definition_zh: 影响；作用；影响力；有影响的人或事
definition_en: the power to change how someone thinks or acts, or to affect events
core_image: 一股看不见的水流，把船慢慢带向旁边
scene: 老师的一句话，学生记了一辈子。His teacher had a lasting influence on his choice of career.
sceneCN: 这里 influence 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对他人想法或选择的作用）；句意是他的老师对他的职业选择有持久的影响。

pos.zh: 名词：影响；影响力；有影响的人或事
动词：影响；对……起作用

derivatives.zh: 加 -ial，义为「有影响力的」
同出意大利语 influenza，义为「流行性感冒」
加 -ed，义为「受影响的」
加 un-，义为「未受影响的」

senses.title: Power over people
senses.definition: the power that one person or thing has to change others
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物改变他人的力量
senses.example: Parents have a strong influence on young children.
senses.exampleCN: 父母对幼小的孩子有很强的影响。
senses.why: The Latin word was about an invisible fluid flowing in, and that is what influence feels like.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词原指流入的无形流体，而影响给人的感觉正是如此。

senses.title: A person or thing that affects
senses.definition: someone or something that changes others
senses.definitionCN: 改变他人的某个人或某件事
senses.example: She was the biggest influence on my writing.
senses.exampleCN: 她是对我写作影响最大的人。
senses.why: The abstract power is then attached to the person who carries it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的力量随后被安放在携带它的人身上。

senses.title: The act of affecting events
senses.definition: the effect that conditions, money or groups have on events
senses.definitionCN: 条件、资金或团体对事件的作用
senses.example: The climate has an influence on what farmers can grow.
senses.exampleCN: 气候影响着农民能种什么。
senses.why: Beyond people, whole conditions can steer outcomes the same way.
senses.whyCN: 超越个人，整体条件也以同样的方式左右结果。

senses.title: To affect someone
senses.definition: to change the way someone thinks or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 改变某人的想法或行为
senses.example: Advertising influences what we buy.
senses.exampleCN: 广告影响着我们买什么。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb keeps the same picture of something flowing in.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，仍是某种东西流进来的画面。

senses.title: Political or social power
senses.definition: the ability to affect decisions in public life
senses.definitionCN: 影响公共决策的能力
senses.example: The group used its influence to block the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 该团体动用它的影响力阻止了这项计划。
senses.why: In public affairs the word names the practical power behind decisions.
senses.whyCN: 在公共事务中，这个词指决策背后的实际力量。

intro.en: Influence comes from Medieval Latin influentia, a flowing in, from influere, in- plus fluere, to flow.
intro.cn: influence 来自中世纪拉丁语 influentia（流入），出自 influere，即 in- 加 fluere（流动）。

items.en: Fluere meant to flow, and influere meant to flow into.
items.cn: fluere 意为流动，influere 意为流入。

items.en: Astrologers spoke of influentia, an invisible power flowing from the stars into people.
items.cn: 占星家谈 influentia，即从星辰流入人体的无形力量。

items.en: The word entered English through French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: When astrology faded, the word kept the sense of unseen power over people.
items.cn: 占星术衰落之后，这个词保留了「无形支配力」的含义。

items.en: The verb use developed later, from the same noun, in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 动词用法较晚，在十七世纪由同一名词发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fluere family; the near-meaning group holds words of power over others.
note.cn: 形近组收 fluere 词族；近义组收描述对他人的支配力。

entries.definition: Having power to affect others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有影响力的」。

entries.definition: A virus that spreads like an influence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流行性感冒」，同出意大利语 influenza。

entries.definition: A substance that flows.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「流体」，与 fluere 同源。

entries.definition: A change produced by a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效果」，强调结果。

entries.definition: A strong effect or hit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「影响；冲击」，语气更强。

entries.definition: The ability to make things happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「权力；力量」，是更宽泛的说法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of flowing water, then attach the word to teachers and advertising.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子保留流水的画面，再把词与老师、广告相连。

normal.en: Fluere means flow, so influence is literally something flowing into you.
normal.cn: fluere 意为流动，所以 influence 字面上就是有东西流进你身上。

normal.en: The -ence ending makes a noun, and influential is its adjective.
normal.cn: -ence 词尾构成名词，influential 是其形容词。

normal.en: Have an influence on is the standard frame, with on rather than to.
normal.cn: have an influence on 是标准框架，用 on 而不是 to。

normal.en: Under the influence of means being steered while in that state.
normal.cn: under the influence of 意为处在那种状态下被左右。

normal.en: Influenza got its name because people thought the stars sent it flowing in.
normal.cn: influenza 得名是因为人们以为星辰把它送了下来。

abstract.en: Influence is an invisible current: nothing is pushed, yet the boat moves.
abstract.cn: 影响是一道看不见的水流：没有人推，船却动了。

abstract.en: To influence is to change another without touching, which is the quietest form of power.
abstract.cn: 影响是不接触就改变他人，这是最安静的力量形式。

abstract.en: The word once belonged to the stars, and it still suggests something above pouring down.
abstract.cn: 这个词曾属于星辰，至今仍暗示有东西自高处倾下。

examples.en: The book had a strong influence on young readers.
examples.cn: 这本书对年轻读者有很大影响。

examples.en: Do not let bad company influence your choices.
examples.cn: 不要让坏朋友影响你的选择。

examples.en: He used his influence to help the little school.
examples.cn: 他动用自己的影响力帮助那所小学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因福露恩死」——因为福气露了，恩情至死都在影响着他。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 influentia（流入）= in-（进入）+ fluere（流动）；同族词有 influential、fluent、fluid。

sensesIntro.en: From an astrological fluid flowing in, influence moves to power over people, then to the person who has it, to effects on events and finally to a verb of affecting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从占星术里流入的流体出发，influence 走向对人的支配力、有这种力的人、对事件的作用，最后成为表示影响他人的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unseen current pushing a boat sideways.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见的水流把船推向一侧。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: one person's power over another.
branches.cn: 人际线：一个人对另一个人的力量。

branches.en: SOURCE LINE: the one who carries that power.
branches.cn: 来源线：携带这种力量的人。

branches.en: EVENT LINE: climate or money steers results.
branches.cn: 事件线：气候或资金左右结果。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: the noun becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 动作线：名词转为动词。

branches.en: PUBLIC LINE: power that reaches decisions.
branches.cn: 公共线：能影响决策的力量。

intro.en: A noun of flowing, whose -ence ending also appears in fluent and fluid.
intro.cn: 一个表示流动的名词，其 -ence 词尾也见于 fluent 与 fluid。

latinIntro.en: The root fluere, to flow, gives fluent, fluid, flux and the medical influenza.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fluere（流动）产生 fluent、fluid、flux 以及医学词 influenza。

definition_zh: 有影响力的；有势力的；有很大影响的
definition_en: having the power to affect people, decisions or events
core_image: 一个人说话，满屋子的人立刻改变主意
scene: 小镇上的报纸没人敢小看。The local paper has become influential far beyond the town.
sceneCN: 这里 influential 是「有影响力的」（第 1 个义项：能影响他人或决定）；句意是这家地方报纸的影响力已远及镇外。

pos.zh: 形容词：有影响力的；有势力的；有很大影响的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ial，义为「影响」
加 -ly，义为「有影响地」
加否定前缀，义为「无影响力的」
同根词，义为「流行性感冒」

senses.title: Able to affect people
senses.definition: able to change how others think or act
senses.definitionCN: 能改变他人的想法或行为
senses.example: She became one of the most influential teachers in the school.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了学校里最有影响力的老师之一。
senses.why: The -ial ending simply turns influence into a quality someone has.
senses.whyCN: -ial 词尾只是把 influence 变成某人所具备的性质。

senses.title: Able to affect decisions
senses.definition: having power in politics, business or public life
senses.definitionCN: 在政治、商业或公共生活中拥有力量
senses.example: The committee is influential in local politics.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会在地方政治中很有影响力。
senses.why: Power over outcomes, not just opinions, is the second step.
senses.whyCN: 对结果而不只是对意见的支配力，是这个形容词的第二步。

senses.title: A work that shaped others
senses.definition: said of a book, idea or event that changed a whole field
senses.definitionCN: 指改变了整个领域的书、思想或事件
senses.example: This was an influential book on how children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一本关于儿童如何学习的深有影响的书。
senses.why: Things can carry influence too, especially works that others follow.
senses.whyCN: 事物也能携带影响力，尤其是被后人效仿的作品。

senses.title: Having many connections
senses.definition: having wealth or friends who can make things happen
senses.definitionCN: 拥有财富或能办事的人脉
senses.example: His family is influential in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他家在城里很有势力。
senses.why: From real effect the word slides to social weight and connections.
senses.whyCN: 从实际作用出发，这个词滑向社会分量与人脉。

intro.en: Influential is an English adjective formed on influence, from Medieval Latin influentia, a flowing in.
intro.cn: influential 是在 influence 上构成的英语形容词，后者出自中世纪拉丁语 influentia（流入）。

items.en: Influere meant to flow into, from in- plus fluere, to flow.
items.cn: influere 意为流入，由 in- 加 fluere（流动）构成。

items.en: Influentia named the invisible power believed to flow from the stars.
items.cn: influentia 指人们相信从星辰流入的无形力量。

items.en: The noun reached English through French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个名词在十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ial was attached to make an adjective in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪加上后缀 -ial 构成形容词。

items.en: Influential spread widely with talk of influential people and papers in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪谈有影响的人物与报纸，influential 广泛流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fluere family; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of power.
note.cn: 形近组收 fluere 词族；近义组收表示力量与地位的形容词。

entries.definition: The power to affect others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「影响」，是本词的来源。

entries.definition: A virus that once was blamed on the stars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流感」，同出意大利语 influenza。

entries.definition: In a way that has effect.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有影响地」。

entries.definition: Having great power.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强大的」，更笼统。

entries.definition: Of great value or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「重要的」，不必然指影响他人。

entries.definition: Large enough to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「显著的」，强调分量。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the adjective to its noun and to the flowing picture behind both.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把形容词与它的名词以及背后的流水画面相连。

normal.en: Influence plus -ial gives an adjective: full of influence.
normal.cn: influence 加 -ial 得形容词：充满影响力的。

normal.en: Influential is almost always used of people, papers and books, not of weather.
normal.cn: influential 几乎总用于人、报纸与书，而不用来形容天气。

normal.en: Influential in politics means able to steer decisions.
normal.cn: influential in politics 意为能左右决策。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the -flu- of flow, so the word still sounds like water.
normal.cn: 拼写保留流动的 -flu-，这个词听起来仍像水。

normal.en: More influential and most influential handle the comparison.
normal.cn: more influential 与 most influential 承担比较级与最高级。

abstract.en: An influential person is a river others quietly follow.
abstract.cn: 有影响力的人是一条别人默默顺着走的河。

abstract.en: Influence is measured backwards: we see it only in what changed.
abstract.cn: 影响力的度量是回望的：我们只在改变了的东西里看见它。

abstract.en: The word means pouring in, and power that pours never stays in one place.
abstract.cn: 这个词意为灌入，而倾注的力量从不只停在一处。

examples.en: He was an influential member of the committee.
examples.cn: 他是委员会里很有影响力的成员。

examples.en: The report proved influential in changing the law.
examples.cn: 这份报告在改变法律方面被证明很有影响。

examples.en: Few writers have been as influential as she was.
examples.cn: 很少有作家像她那样影响深远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因福露恩少」——因为福气与恩情露得少，才更要靠影响力说话。

root: influence（影响）+ -ial（形容词后缀）；词根为拉丁 fluere（流动）。

sensesIntro.en: Influential turns the flowing-in power into a quality: able to change people, then decisions, then whole fields, and finally social weight.
sensesIntro.cn: influential 把流入的力量变成一种性质：能改变人，然后是决策、整个领域，最后是社会分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker who changes the room in one sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话就让满屋转向的发言者。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: able to change minds.
branches.cn: 人际线：能改变人心。

branches.en: DECISION LINE: able to steer outcomes.
branches.cn: 决策线：能左右结果。

branches.en: WORKS LINE: books and ideas that reshape a field.
branches.cn: 作品线：重塑一个领域的书与思想。

branches.en: STATUS LINE: wealth and connections that carry weight.
branches.cn: 地位线：有分量的财富与人脉。

branches.en: POWER LINE: one unseen force, two directions.
branches.cn: 力量线：同一股无形之力，两个方向。

intro.en: An adjective in -ial formed on the noun of flowing in.
intro.cn: 一个以 -ial 结尾、由「流入」名词构成的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The root fluere, to flow, gives fluent, fluid, flux and influenza.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fluere（流动）产生 fluent、fluid、flux 与 influenza。

definition_zh: 通知；告知；举报；影响（风格）
definition_en: to tell someone officially or clearly about something
core_image: 一封信被送到门口，里面写着要知道的事
scene: 车站的广播突然响起来。Please inform the office if you change your address.
sceneCN: 这里 inform 是「告知」（第 1 个义项：把情况正式告诉别人）；句意是如果改变地址，请告知办公室。

pos.zh: 动词：通知；告知；举报
及物：使了解；赋予特征

derivatives.zh: 加 -ation，义为「信息；消息」
加 -ed，义为「了解情况的」
加 -ative，义为「提供有用信息的」
加 -ant，义为「提供消息的人」

senses.title: To tell officially
senses.definition: to give someone facts they need to know
senses.definitionCN: 把对方需要知道的事实告诉他
senses.example: Please inform us of any change of plan.
senses.exampleCN: 计划如有变动请告知我们。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to give shape, and giving shape to someone's knowledge is informing them.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「赋予形状」，而给一个人的知识赋予形状就是告知他。

senses.title: To report to authorities
senses.definition: to give information about wrongdoing to the police or officials
senses.definitionCN: 向警方或官方提供有关违法行为的消息
senses.example: He informed on his partners to save himself.
senses.exampleCN: 为了自保，他举报了合伙人。
senses.why: Information given to power becomes a report, and the verb narrows to that act.
senses.whyCN: 交给权力的信息就是举报，动词于是收窄到这个动作。

senses.title: To shape a decision
senses.definition: to give the knowledge that shapes a choice or work
senses.definitionCN: 提供塑造选择或作品的知识
senses.example: The survey will inform future policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查将为今后的政策提供依据。
senses.why: Since inform meant to give shape, it also describes knowledge shaping decisions.
senses.whyCN: 由于 inform 本义是赋予形状，它也用来描述知识塑造决策。

senses.title: To fill with a quality
senses.definition: to give a work or action its special character
senses.definitionCN: 赋予作品或行为以特有的性质
senses.example: A quiet sadness informs the whole novel.
senses.exampleCN: 一种静默的忧伤贯穿整部小说。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a form is breathed into a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：把一种形态注入事物之中。

senses.title: To keep informed
senses.definition: to give people continuing news, used in keep informed
senses.definitionCN: 持续向人提供消息，见于 keep informed
senses.example: Keep me informed about the results.
senses.exampleCN: 结果如何随时告诉我。
senses.why: Continuous telling becomes a fixed phrase about staying up to date.
senses.whyCN: 持续的告知形成固定说法，表示保持在最新状态。

intro.en: Inform comes from Latin informare, to shape or give form, from in- plus forma, form.
intro.cn: inform 来自拉丁语 informare（赋予形状），由 in- 加 forma（形状）构成。

items.en: Forma meant shape, and informare meant to give shape to something.
items.cn: forma 意为形状，informare 意为给某物赋予形状。

items.en: The verb also meant to instruct, since teaching shapes the mind.
items.cn: 这个动词也指教导，因为教学塑造心灵。

items.en: The word came into English through French with the sense of teaching.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，带有教导之义。

items.en: By the sixteenth century inform meant to tell facts.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，inform 意为告知事实。

items.en: The sense of giving character survived in literary descriptions.
items.cn: 「赋予特征」的义项在文学描写中留存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the forma family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of telling.
note.cn: 形近组收 forma 词族；近义组收告知类动词。

entries.definition: Facts about something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信息」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: Giving useful facts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「提供有用信息的」。

entries.definition: A shape or a document.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形状；表格」，是词根本身。

entries.definition: To tell officially.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「通知」，语气更正式。

entries.definition: To give information in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告诉」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To make something public.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布」，面向公众。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on forma and on the family of nouns and adjectives built from inform.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 forma 以及由 inform 构成的名词形容词词族。

normal.en: Forma means shape, so to inform is to shape what someone knows.
normal.cn: forma 意为形状，所以 inform 就是塑造别人的认知。

normal.en: Inform someone of something uses of, not about, in careful writing.
normal.cn: inform someone of something 在正式写作中用 of 而不用 about。

normal.en: Keep me informed is the fixed phrase for staying up to date.
normal.cn: keep me informed 是表示随时知情的固定说法。

normal.en: Informative adds -ive: a talk that gives you a lot of facts.
normal.cn: informative 加 -ive：一次给你很多事实的讲座。

normal.en: Inform on someone means to report them, a very different direction.
normal.cn: inform on someone 意为举报某人，方向大不相同。

abstract.en: To inform is to pour facts into a mould the mind already has.
abstract.cn: 告知是把事实倒进心里已有的模子。

abstract.en: Knowledge has a shape, and news is what reshapes it.
abstract.cn: 知识有形状，消息就是重塑它的东西。

abstract.en: The word joins form and news: what we are told gives form to what we think.
abstract.cn: 这个词把形状与消息连在一起：我们被告知的东西塑造着我们怎么想。

examples.en: The school will inform parents of any change.
examples.cn: 学校会把任何变动通知家长。

examples.en: He informed the police about the broken window.
examples.cn: 他把窗户被打破的事报告了警方。

examples.en: Good research should inform the final decision.
examples.cn: 好的研究应当为最终决定提供依据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛母」——因为佛母显灵，消息要赶紧通知众人。

root: 拉丁语 informare（赋予形状）= in-（进入）+ forma（形状）；同族词有 information、informative、form。

sensesIntro.en: Inform starts as giving shape, becomes teaching, then telling facts, and branches into reporting to the police and shaping decisions or works.
sensesIntro.cn: inform 起初是赋予形状，继而指教导，再变为告知事实，并分支为向警方举报，以及为决策或作品提供形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter at the door with the facts inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口一封信，里面装着要知道的事。

branches.en: TELL LINE: facts given to the person who needs them.
branches.cn: 告知线：把事实交给需要的人。

branches.en: REPORT LINE: information handed to power.
branches.cn: 举报线：信息被交给权力。

branches.en: DECISION LINE: knowledge shapes a choice.
branches.cn: 决策线：知识塑造选择。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: a quality shapes a work.
branches.cn: 特征线：某种性质塑造作品。

branches.en: CONTINUITY LINE: staying informed over time.
branches.cn: 持续线：随时间保持知情。

intro.en: A Latin verb of shaping whose family covers news, teaching and form itself.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「赋形」动词，其词族覆盖消息、教导与形状本身。

latinIntro.en: The root forma, shape, gives form, format, reform and information.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 forma（形状）产生 form、format、reform 与 information。

definition_zh: 非正式的；不拘礼的；随意的；口语的
definition_en: relaxed and friendly, not following official rules or ceremony
core_image: 脱下西装换上T恤，大家坐在沙发上聊天
scene: 聚会没有主持，也没有发言顺序。It was an informal dinner, so nobody dressed up.
sceneCN: 这里 informal 是「非正式的」（第 1 个义项：不按礼节与规矩进行）；句意那是顿非正式的晚餐，所以没人盛装打扮。

pos.zh: 形容词：非正式的；不拘礼的；随意的

derivatives.zh: 义为「正式地」，去掉否定前缀后加 -ly
加 -ity，义为「非正式；随意」
加 -ly，义为「非正式地」
去掉否定前缀，义为「正式的」

senses.title: Relaxed in manner
senses.definition: easy and friendly rather than stiff and polite
senses.definitionCN: 轻松友好，而非拘谨客套
senses.example: The interview felt informal and friendly.
senses.exampleCN: 那次面谈感觉随意而友好。
senses.why: In- removes the rules of form, so the word means without ceremony.
senses.whyCN: in- 去掉了形式的规矩，所以这个词意为「没有礼节」。

senses.title: Not official
senses.definition: not arranged according to official rules
senses.definitionCN: 不按官方规定安排
senses.example: They reached an informal agreement over lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在午餐时达成了一项非正式协议。
senses.why: Something can be real without being official, and that is the gap this word fills.
senses.whyCN: 事情可以真实却不正式，这个词正好填补这个空档。

senses.title: Everyday in style
senses.definition: suitable for ordinary rather than special occasions
senses.definitionCN: 适合日常场合而非特殊场合
senses.example: Informal clothes are fine for the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行穿便装就可以。
senses.why: Dress follows ceremony, so clothes too are called informal.
senses.whyCN: 着装跟随礼节，因此衣服也被称为 informal。

senses.title: Spoken in everyday language
senses.definition: using the words people use in ordinary talk
senses.definitionCN: 使用人们日常交谈中的词语
senses.example: Gonna is an informal form of going to.
senses.exampleCN: gonna 是 going to 的口语形式。
senses.why: Language has registers, and the word marks the relaxed one.
senses.whyCN: 语言有语体之分，这个词标示轻松的那一端。

senses.title: Outside the official system
senses.definition: happening outside official structures, as of work or trade
senses.definitionCN: 在官方体系之外进行，如工作或交易
senses.example: Many people work in the informal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 许多人在非正规经济中工作。
senses.why: From manners the word reaches economics, where no contract is registered.
senses.whyCN: 从举止出发，这个词延伸到经济学中无登记合同的地带。

intro.en: Informal puts the Latin negative in- on formal, from Latin formalis, of a form, from forma.
intro.cn: informal 把拉丁否定 in- 加在 formal 上，后者出自拉丁 formalis（属于形式的），源自 forma。

items.en: Forma meant shape, and formalis meant belonging to a form or pattern.
items.cn: forma 意为形状，formalis 意为属于某种形式或范式的。

items.en: Formal later covered what follows set rules and ceremony.
items.cn: formal 后来涵盖遵循既定规则与礼节的事物。

items.en: Formal entered English in the fourteenth century from Latin.
items.cn: formal 在十四世纪由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Informal was formed with in- to name what is free of ceremony.
items.cn: informal 加 in- 而构成，用来指不受礼节约束的事物。

items.en: The sociological phrase informal economy spread in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 社会学用语 informal economy 在二十世纪流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the forma family; the near-meaning group holds words for a relaxed manner.
note.cn: 形近组收 forma 词族；近义组收表示轻松不拘的词。

entries.definition: Following official rules and ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正式的」，与 informal 相对。

entries.definition: The quality of being relaxed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「非正式；随意」。

entries.definition: Facts about something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信息」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Relaxed and not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「随意的」，最接近的日常词。

entries.definition: Not approved by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非官方的」，强调合法性。

entries.definition: Calm and free from tension.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「放松的」，强调人的状态。

normalIntro.en: The hooks pair informal with formal, then mark the -al ending and the social uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 informal 与 formal 对照，再点出 -al 词尾与社会场景。

normal.en: In- means not, so informal is simply the reverse of formal.
normal.cn: in- 表示不，所以 informal 就是 formal 的反面。

normal.en: Both words keep the -al ending of the Latin adjective formalis.
normal.cn: 两词都保留拉丁形容词 formalis 的 -al 词尾。

normal.en: Informal economy names work that no office records.
normal.cn: informal economy 指没有机构登记的劳动。

normal.en: An informal chat is shorter and friendlier than a formal meeting.
normal.cn: an informal chat 比正式会议更短更亲切。

normal.en: The noun is informality, not informalness.
normal.cn: 名词是 informality，而不是 informalness。

abstract.en: Formal is a costume; informal is the person inside it taking it off.
abstract.cn: formal 是一套服装，informal 是里面的人把它脱下。

abstract.en: Informatity is trust expressed in manner: no need for ceremony.
abstract.cn: 非正式是在举止里表达信任：不必走礼数。

abstract.en: The word measures distance: the less ceremony, the closer the people.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量距离：礼节越少，人越近。

examples.en: The meeting was informal and everyone spoke freely.
examples.cn: 那次会议很随意，大家畅所欲言。

examples.en: You can wear informal clothes to the party.
examples.cn: 参加这个聚会可以穿便装。

examples.en: They made an informal arrangement to share the cost.
examples.cn: 他们非正式地约定分摊费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛帽」——因为佛帽一摘，人就显得不拘礼节、很随意。

root: 拉丁否定前缀 in-（不）+ formal（正式的），formal 出自拉丁 formalis（形式的）。

sensesIntro.en: Informal simply removes form from formal: relaxed manners, unofficial deals, everyday clothes, spoken language and work outside official systems.
sensesIntro.cn: informal 只是把 formal 的「形式」去掉：轻松的举止、非官方约定、日常衣着、口语，以及官方体系外的劳动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ties loosened, jackets off, people talking freely.
core.cn: 核心意象：松开领带、脱下外套，人们随意交谈。

branches.en: MANNER LINE: easy and friendly behaviour.
branches.cn: 举止线：轻松友好的行为。

branches.en: OFFICIAL LINE: real but not registered.
branches.cn: 官方线：真实但未登记。

branches.en: DRESS LINE: clothes for ordinary days.
branches.cn: 衣着线：日常穿着。

branches.en: LANGUAGE LINE: the spoken register.
branches.cn: 语言线：口语语体。

branches.en: SYSTEM LINE: activity outside formal structures.
branches.cn: 体系线：正式结构之外的活动。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective of form, the pattern behind many English opposites.
intro.cn: 一个加在「形式的」形容词前的否定前缀，构成英语中大量反义词。

latinIntro.en: The root forma, shape, gives formal, format, reform and uniform.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 forma（形状）产生 formal、format、reform 与 uniform。

definition_zh: 信息；资料；消息；情报
definition_en: facts or details about someone or something
core_image: 抽屉里一叠整理好的卡片，每张写着一件事
scene: 出发前先查清路线和时刻。We need more information about the trains before we book.
sceneCN: 这里 information 是「信息、资料」（第 1 个义项：关于某事的事实）；句意是订票之前我们需要更多关于列车的信息。

pos.zh: 名词：信息；资料；消息；情报（不可数）

forms.label: 无变化（不可数名词，无复数）

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ation，义为「通知；告知」
加 -ive，义为「信息量大的」
加 -ed，义为「知情的」
加 -al，义为「信息性的」

senses.title: Facts about something
senses.definition: facts and details about a subject
senses.definitionCN: 关于某个主题的事实与细节
senses.example: The leaflet gives information about opening times.
senses.exampleCN: 这份传单提供了开放时间的信息。
senses.why: The noun names what informing delivers: knowledge shaped into usable facts.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名告知所交付的东西：被整理成可用事实的知识。

senses.title: News about people
senses.definition: news or details about a person
senses.definitionCN: 关于某人的消息与细节
senses.example: Police are still collecting information about the incident.
senses.exampleCN: 警方仍在收集关于这一事件的消息。
senses.why: From subjects the word turns to persons and events.
senses.whyCN: 从主题出发，这个词转向人物与事件。

senses.title: Data in a system
senses.definition: data stored and processed by computers or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或机构存储与处理的数据
senses.example: The information is kept on a secure server.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信息保存在一台安全的服务器上。
senses.why: Modern technology makes information something stored rather than remembered.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术让信息成为被存储的东西，而不再是被记住的东西。

senses.title: Intelligence for decisions
senses.definition: facts gathered for official or military use
senses.definitionCN: 为官方或军事用途收集的事实
senses.example: The agency gathered information on the group for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机构多年来收集该团体的情报。
senses.why: Information gathered for power takes the name intelligence, but the noun stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 为权力收集的信息叫作情报，但用的仍是这个名词。

senses.title: The act of informing
senses.definition: the act of giving someone facts, mainly in older use
senses.definitionCN: 把事实告知他人的行为，多见于较老用法
senses.example: Thank you for your information about the road closure.
senses.exampleCN: 谢谢你告知道路封闭的消息。
senses.why: The -ation ending keeps the old sense of the action as well as its result.
senses.whyCN: -ation 词尾既保留动作的旧义，也保留其结果。

intro.en: Information comes from Latin informatio, a shaping or an outline, from informare, to give form.
intro.cn: information 来自拉丁语 informatio（塑造、勾勒），出自 informare（赋予形状）。

items.en: Informatio meant the act of giving shape or forming an idea.
items.cn: informatio 意为赋予形状或形成观念的行为。

items.en: It also named an outline, the shape of a plan or a case.
items.cn: 它也指轮廓，即某项计划或案件的概要。

items.en: The word passed into French and then into English in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个词经法语在中古时期进入英语。

items.en: Informatio became information, meaning instruction and later news.
items.cn: informatio 变为 information，先指教导，后指消息。

items.en: In the twentieth century information became a technical word for data.
items.cn: 二十世纪 information 成为指数据的技术词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the inform family; the near-meaning group holds words for facts and news.
note.cn: 形近组收 inform 词族；近义组收事实与消息类名词。

entries.definition: To tell someone facts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告知」，是本词的原形。

entries.definition: Giving useful facts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「信息量大的」。

entries.definition: A complete change of form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转变」，与 form 同根。

entries.definition: Facts collected for analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据」，偏技术意味。

entries.definition: Recent events reported to people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「新闻」，强调新近发生。

entries.definition: What a person understands and knows.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「知识」，比 information 更内在。

normalIntro.en: The hooks note the -ation ending, the uncountable grammar and the split from data and news.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子留意 -ation 词尾、不可数语法，以及与 data、news 的区别。

normal.en: Inform plus -ation makes the noun of the thing given when you inform.
normal.cn: inform 加 -ation 构成名词，指告知时给出的东西。

normal.en: Information is uncountable: a piece of information, never informations.
normal.cn: information 不可数：a piece of information，绝不说 informations。

normal.en: Information technology puts the word at the centre of modern work.
normal.cn: information technology 把这个词放在现代工作的中心。

normal.en: Knowledge lives in a person, information lives in a note or a file.
normal.cn: knowledge 住在人心里，information 住在便条或文件里。

normal.en: The old sense survives in thank you for your information.
normal.cn: 旧义仍留在 thank you for your information 这样的说法里。

abstract.en: Information is form given to facts so that others can carry them.
abstract.cn: 信息是给事实赋予的形状，让别人也能带走。

abstract.en: The word once meant shaping, and a mind is still shaped by what it receives.
abstract.cn: 这个词曾指塑造，而头脑至今仍被它接收的东西塑造。

abstract.en: Too much information is not knowledge; it is only more shape.
abstract.cn: 信息太多并不等于知识，只是更多形状而已。

examples.en: Please send me information about the course.
examples.cn: 请把关于这门课程的信息发给我。

examples.en: He gave the police information about the car.
examples.cn: 他向警方提供了关于那辆车的信息。

examples.en: All personal information is kept safe.
examples.cn: 所有个人信息都被妥善保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因佛没神」——因为拜佛没显灵，只好自己收集信息资料。

root: inform（告知）+ -ation（名词后缀）；词根为拉丁 forma（形状）。

sensesIntro.en: Information keeps the old sense of shaping while becoming facts about subjects, news about people, stored data and gathered intelligence.
sensesIntro.cn: information 保留「塑造」的旧义，同时演变为关于主题的事实、关于人物的消息、存储的数据以及收集的情报。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of cards each holding one fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠卡片，每张写着一件事实。

branches.en: FACT LINE: details about a subject.
branches.cn: 事实线：关于某主题的细节。

branches.en: NEWS LINE: what is said about people.
branches.cn: 消息线：关于人们的说法。

branches.en: DATA LINE: facts stored in systems.
branches.cn: 数据线：存于系统中的事实。

branches.en: POWER LINE: facts gathered for decisions.
branches.cn: 权力线：为决策收集的事实。

branches.en: SHAPING LINE: the act of informing and what it leaves.
branches.cn: 塑造线：告知的行为及其留下的东西。

intro.en: The noun of informing, built with the productive suffix -ation.
intro.cn: 表示告知的名词，由能产后缀 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The root forma, shape, gives formation, format and transformation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 forma（形状）产生 formation、format 与 transformation。

definition_zh: 基础设施；基础结构；公共设施；下部结构；基础架构
definition_en: the basic physical and organizational structures and facilities that a society or enterprise needs in order to operate
core_image: 路面之下看不见的管网：水管、电缆、排水沟、光纤一层层铺在土里，托住上面所有的房子和车流
scene: 这里指「基础设施」。 The city's infrastructure was laid a century ago and cannot carry today's traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 infrastructure 是「基础设施」总称（第 1 个义项：社会运转所依赖的道路、供水等基本系统）；句意：这座城市的基础设施是一个世纪前铺设的，已承载不了今天的车流。图中可辨识物件：老旧水管、道路剖面、施工围挡。

pos.zh: 基础设施；基础结构；公共设施；下部结构

derivatives.zh: 基础设施的；基础结构的
上部结构；上层建筑
下部结构；基础
网络基础设施
绿色基础设施

senses.title: The basic systems a society runs on
senses.titleCN: 基础设施：社会运转所依赖的基本系统
senses.definition: the roads, bridges, water supply, power lines, and similar works that a country or city needs to function
senses.definitionCN: 国家或城市运转所需的道路、桥梁、供水、电力线路等工程设施
senses.example: The storm damaged infrastructure across three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴破坏了三个省的基础设施。
senses.why: Infra means 'below' and structura means 'building'. The word names the layer beneath a society's visible buildings, the works that must exist before other works can stand.
senses.whyCN: infra 意为「在下」，structura 意为「建造」。这个词命名的是社会可见建筑之下的那一层，是其他工程能够立起来之前必须先存在的东西。

senses.title: The substructure below the surface
senses.titleCN: 下部结构：地面之下承重的那一层
senses.definition: the lower part of a structure, especially the foundations and works below ground level
senses.definitionCN: 结构的下部，尤指地面以下的根基与工程部分
senses.example: The bridge's infrastructure was reinforced with concrete piles.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的下部结构用混凝土桩加固过。
senses.why: In nineteenth-century engineering, infrastructure was the substructure of a railway or road, the part under the visible surface. The French technical coinage is generally associated with this need.
senses.whyCN: 在 19 世纪的工程语境中，infrastructure 指铁路或道路的下部结构，即可见表面之下的部分。一般认为这一法语技术词正是为这种需要而造的。

senses.title: The pipes and wires of daily life
senses.titleCN: 公用设施：水、电、燃气、排污那套管网
senses.definition: the public utilities such as water, gas, electricity, and sewerage that serve homes and businesses
senses.definitionCN: 为家庭与企业服务的水、燃气、电力、排污等公用事业设施
senses.example: The neighbourhood lacks basic infrastructure such as clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个街区缺乏清洁供水等基本公用设施。
senses.why: Utilities are the pipes and wires through which water, gas, and power flow. They are infrastructure in its most literal below-the-street form.
senses.whyCN: 公用事业就是水、燃气与电力流经的管道和电线。它们是最字面意义上的「街道之下」的基础设施。

senses.title: The frame beneath an organization
senses.titleCN: 基础架构：一个组织看不见的骨架
senses.definition: the systems, procedures, and roles that support the work of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 支撑一个组织运作的制度、程序与角色体系
senses.example: The company rebuilt its management infrastructure after the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 合并后，公司重建了管理基础架构。
senses.why: An organization also has a layer beneath its visible activities: procedures, systems, and roles. The metaphor imports the engineering image into management.
senses.whyCN: 一个组织在其可见活动之下也有一层：程序、制度与角色。这个隐喻把工程的意象搬进了管理。

senses.title: The networks behind computing
senses.titleCN: 信息基础设施：服务器、电缆与协议
senses.definition: the hardware, networks, and systems on which computing and communications depend
senses.definitionCN: 计算与通信所依赖的硬件、网络与系统
senses.example: universities share a high-speed information infrastructure
senses.exampleCN: 多所大学共享一套高速信息基础设施。
senses.why: Digital networks are the new pipes: servers, cables, protocols. The name follows because nothing above can run without them.
senses.whyCN: 数字网络是新的管道：服务器、电缆、协议。这个名字跟着来了，因为上面的一切离开它们都运行不了。

senses.title: Permanent military installations
senses.titleCN: 军事设施：军队长期使用的固定基地
senses.definition: the permanent bases, airfields, depots, and other fixed installations used by armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装部队使用的永久基地、机场、仓库等固定设施
senses.example: The treaty limited the infrastructure allowed near the border.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约限制了边境附近允许设置的军事设施。
senses.why: Permanent bases, airfields, and depots are the fixed layer under military operations, which move above them.
senses.whyCN: 永久基地、机场与仓库是军事行动之下的固定层，行动在其上移动。

senses.title: The base of an economy
senses.titleCN: 经济基础设施：市场赖以运转的交通与能源
senses.definition: the transport, power, and communication systems on which economic activity depends
senses.definitionCN: 经济活动所依赖的交通、能源与通信系统
senses.example: Weak infrastructure raises the cost of moving goods.
senses.exampleCN: 薄弱的基础设施提高了货物运输成本。
senses.why: Economists widened the term to the transport, power, and communication base on which markets depend. The metaphor is still a supporting layer.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这个词扩展到市场所依赖的交通、能源与通信基础。隐喻仍然是一层承托之物。

senses.title: The base of social life
senses.titleCN: 社会基础设施：学校、医院与公园
senses.definition: the schools, hospitals, parks, and community services that support social well-being
senses.definitionCN: 支撑社会福祉的学校、医院、公园与社区服务
senses.example: Hospitals and schools are part of social infrastructure.
senses.exampleCN: 医院和学校属于社会基础设施。
senses.why: Schools, hospitals, and parks form the layer that supports social life; the word adds a social sector to the physical list.
senses.whyCN: 学校、医院与公园构成支撑社会生活的那一层；这个词在实物的清单上又加进了社会部门。

senses.title: The enduring base of any system
senses.titleCN: 根基：任何体系底下那层不易更换的东西
senses.definition: the underlying foundation of an idea, system, or activity, often used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 观念、体系或活动底下那层基础，常用于比喻
senses.example: Trust is the infrastructure of a working team.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是一个能运作的团队的基础。
senses.why: In general use, any enduring base of an idea or system can be called its infrastructure, even when nothing is made of concrete.
senses.whyCN: 在一般用法中，任何观念或体系持久的底座都可以称为它的 infrastructure，哪怕没有一点混凝土。

intro.en: Infrastructure joins Latin infra 'below' to structura 'a building, arrangement', from struere 'to build'. The word was coined in nineteenth-century engineering to name the substructure under a railway, then widened to the whole supporting base of a society.
intro.cn: infrastructure 把拉丁 infra「在下」与 structura「建造物、构造」连接起来，后者来自 struere「建造」。这个词在 19 世纪的工程语境中被造出，指铁路之下的下部结构，随后扩展到整个社会的承托底座。

items.en: infra meant 'below, beneath'. It belongs to the same family as inferus 'lower' and inferior, and is not the negative prefix in-; the two prefixes are different morphemes that happen to look alike.
items.cn: infra 意为「在下、低于」。它与 inferus「更低的」、inferior 同族，并不是否定前缀 in-；这两个前缀只是长得像，实为不同语素。

items.en: struere meant 'to pile up, build'. Its noun structura named a building or the way parts are put together, the same base seen in structure, construct, and instruct.
items.cn: struere 意为「堆积、建造」。其名词 structura 指建筑物或各部分的组合方式，同一词基见于 structure、construct、instruct。

items.en: The compound infra- plus structure is generally attributed to nineteenth-century French engineering, where it named the substructure beneath a railway or road. The exact first writer is not certain.
items.cn: infra- 加 structure 这一复合词一般认为出自 19 世纪法国工程语境，用来指铁路或道路之下的下部结构。最早由谁写下并不确定。

items.en: English borrowed the term in the late nineteenth century, still in the civil-engineering sense of the layer below the visible surface.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪末借入该词，仍保留土木工程义，指可见表面之下的那一层。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century, military and political usage applied infrastructure to permanent bases and installations, the fixed layer under moving operations.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶，军事与政治用法把 infrastructure 用于永久基地与设施，即流动行动之下的固定层。

items.en: Later the word spread to economic, social, and digital systems. Each new field kept the same picture: a base that must be in place before anything above it can work.
items.cn: 后来这个词扩展到经济、社会与数字系统。每个新领域都保留同一幅图：一层必须先就位、上面的东西才能运转的底座。

note.en: The first group shares Latin struere or the prefix infra; instruction looks close but uses in- 'into', a different prefix. The second group holds words for facilities or bases that overlap in use but not in image.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁 struere 或前缀 infra；instruction 形似，却用了另一个前缀 in-「向内」。第二组是设施或基础类词，用法重叠但意象不同。

entries.definition: a building or the way parts are arranged. It is the plain noun behind infrastructure, without the infra- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物或各部分的组合方式。它是 infrastructure 背后不带 infra- 前缀的普通名词。

entries.definition: the part of a structure above the base or above a deck. super- 'above' is the mirror of infra- 'below'.
entries.definitionCN: 结构基础之上或甲板之上的部分。super-「在上」正是 infra-「在下」的镜像。

entries.definition: the foundations or lower part of a building. sub- 'under' and infra- 'below' point to the same layer from different roots.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑的根基或下部。sub-「在下」与 infra-「在下」从不同词根指向同一层。

entries.definition: teaching or an order. It is in- 'into' plus struere 'build': building knowledge into a mind, not building below a road.
entries.definitionCN: 教导；指令。它是 in-「向内」加 struere「建造」：把知识建进头脑，而不是在道路下面建造。

entries.definition: buildings, equipment, or services provided for a particular purpose. Facilities are countable items; infrastructure is the connected base they sit on.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途提供的建筑、设备或服务。facilities 是可数的单项，infrastructure 是它们所坐落的连成一片的底座。

entries.definition: public services such as water, gas, and electricity. They are one sector of infrastructure, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 水、燃气、电力等公共服务。它们是基础设施的一个部门，而不是全部。

entries.definition: a supporting structure of ideas or rules. It matches the organizational sense of infrastructure but usually has no physical layer.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑性的观念或规则结构。它对应 infrastructure 的组织义，但通常没有物理层。

entries.definition: the solid base on which a building or an idea rests. It is the base, while infrastructure is the whole system of bases and services.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑或观念所依托的坚固底座。它指底座本身，infrastructure 则指整套底座与服务系统。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent compound: infra 'below' plus structure 'build'. Everything else is the same image applied to pipes, organizations, networks, and ideas.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是透明的复合词：infra「在下」加 structure「建造」。其余义项都是同一幅图用在管道、组织、网络与观念上。

normal.en: infra 'below' + structure 'building': infrastructure is the building that lies below the building you can see.
normal.cn: infra「在下」+ structure「建造物」：infrastructure 就是躺在那栋看得见的建筑下面的建筑。

normal.en: infra is related to inferior 'lower', not to the negative in-; do not read it as 'not structure'.
normal.cn: infra 与 inferior「更低的」同族，与否定前缀 in- 无关；不要把它读成「不是结构」。

normal.en: The stru- root recurs in structure, construct, instruct, destroy: all are about putting up or pulling down a build.
normal.cn: stru- 词根在 structure、construct、instruct、destroy 中重现：都与搭起或拆掉一个建造物有关。

normal.en: Water pipes under a street, servers under a website, procedures under a company: each is the layer that must exist first.
normal.cn: 街道下的水管、网站下的服务器、公司下的流程：每一样都是必须先存在的那一层。

normal.en: The word began with railways, moved to armies, then to economies and the internet without changing its picture.
normal.cn: 这个词从铁路开始，转到军队，再转到经济与互联网，图景始终没变。

abstract.en: Think of a tree: the canopy is what you see, but the root system is its infrastructure, and it is wider than the crown.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树：树冠是你看见的，根系就是它的基础设施，而且比树冠更宽。

abstract.en: Think of a stage: the actors are visible, the scaffolding and trapdoors are the infrastructure that lets the play happen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个舞台：演员是看得见的，脚手架与活动地板就是让戏能发生的基础设施。

abstract.en: Think of a city at night: the lights show the surface, but the cables feeding them run unseen beneath.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里的城市：灯光显示表面，给它们供电的电缆却在下面看不见地延伸。

examples.en: Decades of underinvestment left the railway infrastructure close to collapse.
examples.cn: 数十年的投资不足让铁路基础设施濒临崩溃。

examples.en: The agency classified the power grid as critical infrastructure.
examples.cn: 该机构把电网列为关键基础设施。

examples.en: A reliable digital infrastructure is now as important as roads to a new firm.
examples.cn: 对新公司而言，可靠的数字基础设施如今和道路一样重要。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: infra（在下）+ structure（建造物）——看得见的城市下面还有一层看不见的建造物：管道、电缆、地基，这就是「基础设施」；组织与网络的底层架构也借用了这幅图。

root: 拉丁 infra「在下、低于」（与 inferior「更低的」同源，注意不是否定前缀 in-）+ 拉丁 structura「建造、构造」← struere「建造、堆积」。一般认为该复合词出自 19 世纪法语工程术语，原指铁路、道路的「下部结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one picture: the layer below that carries the layer above. The layer may be made of pipes, concrete, procedures, servers, or trust.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都守住一幅图：下面那一层承托上面那一层。这一层可以是管道、混凝土、程序、服务器，也可以是信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unseen lower layer that carries everything built above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层看不见的下层，承托着上面建起的一切。

branches.en: PHYSICAL BASE: the works a society needs, and the utilities that run beneath its streets.
branches.cn: 物理底座：社会所需的工程，以及在其街道之下运行的公用设施。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERING LAYER: the substructure under a road, bridge, or railway.
branches.cn: 工程层：道路、桥梁或铁路之下的下部结构。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE FRAME: the systems under an organization, and the base of any idea or activity.
branches.cn: 看不见的框架：组织之下的制度，以及任何观念或活动的底座。

branches.en: NETWORKS THAT CARRY AN ECONOMY: computing systems, and the transport and power base of markets.
branches.cn: 承载经济的网络：计算系统，以及市场的交通与能源底座。

branches.en: INSTALLATIONS FOR A SOCIETY: fixed military bases, and the schools and hospitals that support social life.
branches.cn: 社会的设施：固定的军事基地，以及支撑社会生活的学校与医院。

intro.en: Infrastructure is a compound of the Latin prefix infra- and the noun structure. Both halves are still readable in English, which is why the word can be extended to organizations and software without losing its image.
intro.cn: infrastructure 是拉丁前缀 infra- 与名词 structure 的复合词。两半在英语里仍可辨认，所以这个词能扩展到组织与软件而不丢失意象。

latinIntro.en: infra 'below' belongs with inferus and inferior; struere 'to build' yields structura and a large English family: structure, construct, instruct, destroy. The prefix in- in instruct is 'into', not infra.
latinIntro.cn: infra「在下」与 inferus、inferior 同族；struere「建造」产生 structura 以及庞大的英语词族：structure、construct、instruct、destroy。instruct 里的 in- 是「向内」，不是 infra。

items.meaning: the lower works on which a society or system depends
items.meaningCN: 社会或体系所依赖的下层工程与设施
items.example: The flood exposed how fragile the infrastructure was.
items.exampleCN: 洪水暴露出基础设施多么脆弱。

items.example: The plan faces infrastructural and legal obstacles.
items.exampleCN: 该计划面临基础设施与法律上的障碍。

items.meaning: the part built above the base
items.meaningCN: 建于基础之上的上部结构
items.example: Steel cables tie the superstructure to the piers.
items.exampleCN: 钢索把上部结构系在桥墩上。

items.example: Workers inspected the substructure for cracks.
items.exampleCN: 工人检查了下部结构有无裂缝。

items.meaning: a building; the arrangement of parts
items.example: The structure survived the earthquake.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑在地震中幸存下来。

items.meaning: to build knowledge into a mind; to teach
items.example: The coach instructed the team on the new formation.
items.exampleCN: 教练指导球队使用新阵型。

items.meaning: to build by putting parts together
items.example: They constructed a footbridge over the stream.
items.exampleCN: 他们在溪上建了一座人行桥。

items.meaning: the tearing down of a built thing
items.example: The flood caused widespread destruction.
items.exampleCN: 洪水造成了大范围破坏。

items.meaning: the networks and systems behind computing
items.meaningCN: 计算背后的网络与系统；网络基础设施
items.example: The lab applied for funds to upgrade its cyberinfrastructure.
items.exampleCN: 实验室申请资金升级网络基础设施。

latinEntries.meaning: a building; the way parts are put together

definition_zh: 成分；原料；（成功的）要素
definition_en: one of the substances that are combined to make a food, a product, or a successful result
core_image: 案板上一字排开的几样材料，正等着被倒进同一只锅里
scene: 厨房的台面上摊着食谱和一堆还没切的菜。The last ingredient was a spoonful of honey, stirred in at the very end.
sceneCN: 这里 ingredient 是「原料、成分」（第 1 个义项：混合制成食物或产品的材料之一）；句意为最后一样原料是一勺蜂蜜，在最后时刻拌了进去。图中可辨识物件：案板、刀、蜂蜜罐。

pos.zh: 名词：成分；原料；要素

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀构成，义为「就成分而言」
由本词加 list 构成的短语名词，义为「配料表」
由本词加动名词构成，义为「配料标注」

senses.title: Something put into a mixture
senses.definition: one of the substances that are combined to make a dish, a medicine, or a manufactured product
senses.definitionCN: 混合起来做成菜肴、药物或工业制品的物质之一
senses.example: Flour is the main ingredient in this bread.
senses.exampleCN: 面粉是这种面包的主要原料。
senses.why: Latin ingredi means to step into; an ingredient is what steps into the pot or the formula from outside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ingredi 意为「走进去」；ingredient 就是从外面走进锅里或配方里的那样东西。

senses.title: A part of a result
senses.definition: a quality or element that helps to produce a particular result or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 有助于产生某种结果的品质或要素
senses.example: Patience is a key ingredient of good teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是优秀教学的关键要素。
senses.why: The kitchen image travels: anything that steps into a result and helps form it counts as an ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 厨房的意象被搬了过来：凡是走进某个结果并参与构成它的东西，都算 ingredient。

intro.en: Ingredient is a Latin present participle that English borrowed whole; nothing was added or taken away.
intro.cn: ingredient 是英语整体借来的拉丁语现在分词，拼写几乎原样保留。

items.en: The root gradior meant "to walk, step", and it produced gradus "step" as well.
items.cn: 词根 gradior 意为「行走、迈步」，还生出 gradus「步、台阶」。

items.en: In- "into" plus gradi "to step" gave ingredi, "to step into, enter".
items.cn: in-「向内」与 gradi「迈步」合成了 ingredi，意为「走进、进入」。

items.en: The present participle ingrediens meant "entering", and was used of things that go into a mixture.
items.cn: 现在分词 ingrediens 意为「正进入的」，被用来指进入混合物中的东西。

items.en: English took the stem ingredient- directly from Latin in the fifteenth century, first in medical writing.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪直接从拉丁语取用词干 ingredient-，最初见于医学文献。

items.en: Cooking and industry later made it the everyday word for any stuff that goes into a product.
items.cn: 后来烹饪与工业让它成了指任何投入制品的材料的日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same stepping root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for what goes into a mixture.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「迈步」词根构成的词；近义组收其他表示「混合物中的东西」的词。

entries.definition: A slope or a gradual change of colour, built on the same root for step.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坡度、渐变」，词根同样是「步」。

entries.definition: Someone who has stepped through all the stages of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「毕业生」，指走完了全部阶段的人。

entries.definition: A step on a scale, such as a rank or a mark.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「等级、分数」，指阶梯上的一级。

entries.definition: A part of a machine or system, usually technical in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部件、组件」，多用于机械或系统，语气偏技术。

entries.definition: A basic part of a whole, wider than ingredient and often abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「要素、元素」，范围比 ingredient 宽，常指抽象成分。

entries.definition: The stuff something is made from, especially in manufacture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「材料」，多指制造某物所用的物质。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ingredi is to step into: an ingredient steps into the pot.
normal.cn: ingredi 是「走进去」：ingredient 就是走进锅里的那样东西。

normal.en: The same root gives gradient and grade, all about steps.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 gradient、grade，都与「步、台阶」有关。

normal.en: Read the list of ingredients before you buy the packet.
normal.cn: 买包装食品前先看配料表。

normal.en: The main ingredient of a dish is rarely the cheapest one.
normal.cn: 一道菜的主要原料往往不是最便宜的那样。

normal.en: Patience is a key ingredient of good teaching.
normal.cn: 耐心是优秀教学的关键要素。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway into a pot: only the things allowed to step in end up inside.
abstract.cn: 想象锅上有一道门：只有获准踏入的东西才会进到里面。

abstract.en: An ingredient is never alone; it is defined by the company it keeps.
abstract.cn: 原料从不孤单，它的身份由与它同处的其他材料决定。

abstract.en: Results are cooked too: character, timing and luck are ingredients of success.
abstract.cn: 结果也是「炖」出来的：性格、时机与运气都是成功的配料。

examples.en: Mix all the dry ingredients in a large bowl.
examples.cn: 把全部干性原料放进大碗里混合。

examples.en: Trust is the most important ingredient in a partnership.
examples.cn: 信任是合作关系里最重要的要素。

examples.en: The label lists every ingredient in small print.
examples.cn: 标签用小字列出了每一种成分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因贵点」——因原料贵一点，做出来的菜才值钱

root: 拉丁语 ingredi「走进」由 in-「向内」+ gradi「迈步」构成，词根 gradior 又生出 gradus「步、台阶」（grade、gradual、gradient 同源）。现在分词 ingrediens 指「进入混合物中的东西」，英语十五世纪直接取用词干 ingredient-。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: what physically steps into a dish or product, and what figuratively steps into a result.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：实际走进菜肴或产品的东西，以及比喻意义上走进某个结果的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of materials waits at the edge of a pot, ready to step in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排材料在锅边等着踏进去。

branches.en: THE POT: whatever steps into the mixture counts as an ingredient.
branches.cn: 锅这条线：凡是走进混合物的都是 ingredient。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the same word lists what a medicine or a packet contains.
branches.cn: 标签这条线：同一个词也用来列明药物或包装食品里含有什么。

branches.en: THE RESULT: patience, timing and trust step into success as well.
branches.cn: 结果这条线：耐心、时机与信任同样走进成功。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT: an ingredient is always one part of a whole, never the whole.
branches.cn: 抽象这条线：ingredient 永远是整体的一部分，而不是整体。

branches.en: THE LINK: the concrete and the abstract senses share the idea of entering and combining.
branches.cn: 连接线：具体义与抽象义共享「进入并合成」的观念。

intro.en: Ingredient is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin stepping root, with a participle ending English kept intact.
intro.cn: ingredient 由拉丁语前缀与「迈步」词根构成，英语保留了分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradior, gradi and ingredi are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradior、gradi 与 ingredi 均有记录，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

items.example: It marks the movement towards the inside.
The verb supplies the image of a step.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「迈步」的意象。

items.example: The compound was the source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是本词的来源。

items.example: It gave English grade and gradual.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语 grade 与 gradual。

items.example: It keeps the word a participle in form.
items.exampleCN: 它让这个词在形式上保持分词。

items.example: Built on the same root with another ending.

items.meaning: to finish a course of study
items.example: The learner has stepped through every stage.
items.exampleCN: 学习者走完了每一个阶段。

items.example: The root survives again through Old French.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根又经古法语留存下来。

definition_zh: 居民；住户；（某地的）栖息动物
definition_en: a person or animal that lives in a particular place
core_image: 山脚下几间亮着灯的屋子，每一间里都有人在过日子
scene: 小镇只有一条街，店铺傍晚就早早关门。Every inhabitant of the island knows the ferry timetable by heart.
sceneCN: 这里 inhabitant 是「居民、住户」（第 1 个义项：居住在某地的人）；句意为岛上的每位居民都把渡船时刻表背得滚瓜烂熟。图中可辨识物件：屋顶、路灯、渡船。

pos.zh: 名词：居民；住户；栖息动物

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀还原，义为「居住于；栖息于」
由动词加过去分词构成，义为「有人居住的」
由动词加否定前缀构成，义为「无人居住的」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「可居住的」

senses.title: A person who lives in a place
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular town, country, or building
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某个城镇、国家或建筑里的人
senses.example: Most inhabitants of the village work in the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 村里大多数居民在田里干活。
senses.why: In- "in" plus habitare "to dwell" gives a person who dwells inside a place.
senses.whyCN: in-「在内」加 habitare「居住」，得到的就是居住在某地之内的人。

senses.title: An animal that lives somewhere
senses.definition: an animal or plant that lives naturally in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区自然生存的动物或植物
senses.example: Bats are the only inhabitants of the cave in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天蝙蝠是这处洞穴里唯一的栖息者。
senses.why: The same image applies to wild creatures: whoever dwells in a place is its inhabitant.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象也适用于野生生物：凡在某地安身者都是它的 inhabitant。

intro.en: Inhabitant comes from a Latin verb for dwelling, and its ending marks the one who does it.
intro.cn: inhabitant 来自拉丁语表示「居住」的动词，词尾标明动作的承担者。

items.en: Habere meant "to have, hold", and habitare grew from it with the sense "to hold a place, to dwell".
items.cn: habere 意为「拥有、持有」，habitare 由它演变而来，义为「占有某处、居住」。

items.en: The frequentative ending -itare gave habitare its repeated, settled flavour of living somewhere.
items.cn: 表示反复的 -itare 词尾让 habitare 带上「长期待在一处」的意味。

items.en: Old French inhabitant supplied the word to English with the -ant ending of a present participle.
items.cn: 古法语 inhabitant 以现在分词词尾 -ant 把这个词送进英语。

items.en: English adopted it in the late Middle Ages, chiefly in legal and geographical writing.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期采用这个词，主要用于法律与地理文献。

items.en: It now covers animals and plants as easily as people, especially when a habitat is described.
items.cn: 如今它既指人，也常指动植物，尤其在描述栖息地时。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root of having and dwelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who live somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「拥有、居住」词根；近义组收表示「住在某地的人」的词。

entries.definition: The natural home of an animal or plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「栖息地」，指动植物的天然家园。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to live in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住于、栖息于」。

entries.definition: A settled way of behaving, from the same root of holding.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习惯」，词根同为「持有」。

entries.definition: Someone who lives in a house or area, often formally recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「居民」，多用于正式登记语境。

entries.definition: A legal member of a state, not just someone living there.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公民」，指法律上的成员，而非仅居住者。

entries.definition: Someone born in a place, rather than merely living there.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「本地人」，强调出生于此。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on habitare and on the phrases the word usually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子建立在 habitare 与这个词的常见搭配之上。

normal.en: Inhabit is to dwell in: an inhabitant is the one dwelling there.
normal.cn: inhabit 是「住在其中」：inhabitant 就是住在里面的人。

normal.en: Habit, habitat and inhabitant all come from a root meaning to hold.
normal.cn: habit、habitat、inhabitant 都出自表示「持有」的词根。

normal.en: Local inhabitants always know the shortest road.
normal.cn: 本地居民总知道最近的那条路。

normal.en: Writers speak of original inhabitants, meaning those who were there first.
normal.cn: 作者们说 original inhabitants，指最早住在那里的那些人。

normal.en: An uninhabited island has no inhabitants at all.
normal.cn: 无人居住的岛上一个居民也没有。

abstract.en: Picture a house with one lit window: the light is the sign that an inhabitant is inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋只亮着一扇窗的房子：那盏灯就是里面有住户的记号。

abstract.en: Inhabitant ties a creature to a place the way a name ties a person to a family.
abstract.cn: inhabitant 把生物与地点连起来，正如名字把人连到家族上。

abstract.en: Every place is defined as much by who dwells there as by what it looks like.
abstract.cn: 一个地方既由它的样子定义，也由住在那里的人定义。

examples.en: The town has fewer than two thousand inhabitants.
examples.cn: 这个镇子居民不到两千人。

examples.en: Foxes are common inhabitants of this forest.
examples.cn: 狐狸是这片森林常见的栖居者。

examples.en: The new road was welcomed by local inhabitants.
examples.cn: 新修的公路受到当地居民欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因海比吞」——海边小屋有人住，因海而居成居民

root: 拉丁语 habitare「居住」来自 habere「拥有、持有」，反复词尾 -itare 表示长期待在一处；拉丁现在分词词干 inhabitant- 经古法语进入英语，-ant 标明「做这件事的人」。同根词有 habit、habitat、inhabit。

sensesIntro.en: One dwelling image serves both senses: a person who lives in a place, and an animal that lives there too.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用同一个「居住」意象：住在某地的人，以及与之为邻的动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house with a single lit window shows that someone dwells inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋只亮着一扇窗的房子说明里面住着人。

branches.en: THE HOUSE: the inhabitant is the one whose daily life fills a dwelling.
branches.cn: 房屋这条线：inhabitant 是日常生活填满一间屋子的那个人。

branches.en: THE TOWN: towns and countries are spoken of as having inhabitants rather than users.
branches.cn: 城镇这条线：说城镇与国家有 inhabitants，而不是使用它们的人。

branches.en: THE WILD: animals and plants are inhabitants of their habitat.
branches.cn: 野生这条线：动植物是它们栖息地的 inhabitants。

branches.en: THE CAVE: the word suits any dweller, including those that never build a house.
branches.cn: 洞穴这条线：这个词适用于任何栖居者，包括从不造房子的那些。

branches.en: THE PLACE: both senses bind a living thing firmly to one spot.
branches.cn: 地点线：两个义项都把生物牢牢绑在某一处。

intro.en: Inhabitant joins a Latin prefix, a Latin root of holding, and a participle ending that names the doer.
intro.cn: inhabitant 由拉丁语前缀、「持有」词根和标明动作承担者的分词词尾合成。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, habitare and the participle inhabitans are recorded; only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere、habitare 及分词 inhabitans 均有记录，只有印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It places the dwelling inside a territory.
items.exampleCN: 它把居住放进某片地域之内。

items.example: The root also gives habit and able.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 habit 与 able。

items.example: It is the direct source of inhabit.
items.exampleCN: 它是 inhabit 的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the verb its settled, lasting sense.
items.exampleCN: 它让动词带上长久停留的意味。

items.example: It turns the verb into a name for a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指人的名词。

items.example: The same root with a different ending.
The verb behind the noun.
A negative prefix marks the empty places.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀标出无人居住之处。

definition_zh: 固有的；与生俱来的；字里隐含的；无法分离的；法律上固有的；材料本身具有的；逻辑上内含的；生物固有的
definition_en: existing as a natural and permanent part of something, so that it cannot be separated from it
core_image: 老屋墙脚总是渗着湿气，刷多少层漆都盖不住，湿气像是从石头里长出来的
scene: 老屋的墙脚总是渗着湿气，刷多少层漆都盖不住，那湿气像是从石头里长出来的。Old stone walls have an inherent dampness that no paint can hide.
sceneCN: 这里指事物本身固有、靠外力去不掉的（第 1 个义项：作为某物天然组成部分而存在）；句意为老石墙自带一种漆也盖不住的潮气。

pos.zh: 固有的；内在的；与生俱来的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「固有地；本质上」
由该形容词的词干加表示状态的名词后缀构成，义为「固有；内在性」
由同一词干加另一表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「固有性」，多用于哲学与法律
由拉丁 inhaerere 直接进入英语，义为「固有于；存在于」，是该词族的动词
同词根加表示「朝向」的前缀构成，义为「附着的；拥护者」，与目标词共享「粘住」的词根

senses.title: Existing as a natural part
senses.titleCN: 作为天然组成部分而存在
senses.definition: belonging to something so completely that it cannot be taken away without changing the thing
senses.definitionCN: 完全属于某物，取走就会改变该物，因而无法去除
senses.example: Every alloy has inherent limits on how far it can bend.
senses.exampleCN: 每种合金在弯曲程度上都有固有的极限。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stick fast inside, so the adjective pictures a quality lodged in the material itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「牢牢粘在里面」，因此这个形容词画出一种卡在材料内部的素质。

senses.title: Present from birth in a person
senses.definition: part of a person's nature from birth rather than acquired by training
senses.definitionCN: 自出生起就是某人天性的一部分，而非训练所得
senses.example: She has an inherent sense of rhythm that lessons only refined.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种与生俱来的节奏感，课程只是把它打磨得更细。
senses.why: What is stuck in a person from the start cannot be attributed to later learning.
senses.whyCN: 从一开始就「粘」在人身上的东西，不能归因于后来的学习。

senses.title: Implied in the meaning of words
senses.definition: contained in the meaning of a term even when it is not stated openly
senses.definitionCN: 即使没有明说，也包含在一个词项的意义之中
senses.example: The word 'alone' carries an inherent suggestion of sadness.
senses.exampleCN: 「独自」这个词本身就隐含一丝悲凉。
senses.why: A meaning can hold another meaning inside it, the same way a substance holds a quality.
senses.whyCN: 一个意义可以把另一个意义包在里面，正如一种物质含有某种性质。

senses.title: A risk that cannot be separated
senses.definition: a danger or weakness built into an activity so that avoiding it would mean abandoning the activity
senses.definitionCN: 活动本身带来的危险或缺陷，避开它就等于放弃这项活动
senses.example: Some risk is inherent in any surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 任何手术都存在某种固有风险。
senses.why: If the risk comes attached to the practice, no amount of care removes it entirely.
senses.whyCN: 若风险随这项实践一同附着而来，再小心也无法彻底去掉它。

senses.title: A right that belongs by office
senses.titleCN: 因职位本身而有的权利
senses.definition: a power or right held because of the nature of an office or a legal position
senses.definitionCN: 因职位或法律地位的性质而拥有的权力或权利
senses.example: The court has an inherent power to control its own process.
senses.exampleCN: 法院拥有管理自身程序的固有权力。
senses.why: Legal English treats certain powers as attached to the office rather than granted by a separate document.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语把某些权力看作附着于职位本身，而不是由另一份文件授予。

senses.title: A property of the material itself
senses.definition: a physical property that comes from the substance, not from how it is shaped or used
senses.definitionCN: 由物质本身而来的物理性质，而非由形状或用途造成
senses.example: Rust resistance is inherent in stainless steel.
senses.exampleCN: 抗锈性是不锈钢本身固有的。
senses.why: Testing separates what the substance brings from what the process adds, and the former is inherent.
senses.whyCN: 检测要把物质自带的与工艺添加的区分开，前者就是固有的。

senses.title: A contradiction contained within
senses.definition: a conflict that follows from the very definition of a system, so it cannot be removed by adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 由体系定义本身推出的冲突，无法靠调整消除
senses.example: Critics point to an inherent contradiction in the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指出这项政策存在内在矛盾。
senses.why: Logic can hold one statement inside another, and a conflict so held is inherent rather than accidental.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑可以把一个陈述包在另一个里，这样被包住的冲突就是内在的，而非偶然的。

senses.title: Defence present from the start
senses.definition: said of biological protection that an organism is born with, as opposed to acquired immunity
senses.definitionCN: 用于生物体天生具备的保护，与后天获得的免疫相对
senses.example: Inherent immunity blocks many bacteria before antibodies form.
senses.exampleCN: 在抗体形成之前，固有免疫就已挡住许多细菌。
senses.why: The body's first line is already in place, so medicine calls it inherent rather than learned.
senses.whyCN: 身体的第一道防线早已就位，因此医学称它为固有的，而不是后天学来的。

intro.en: Inherent comes from Latin inhaerere 'to stick in', built on in- 'in' and haerere 'to stick, to cling'. Its participle inhaerens gave the adjective, which English took in the seventeenth century. The same root yields adhere and hesitate.
intro.cn: inherent 来自拉丁 inhaerere「粘在里面」，由 in-「在内」与 haerere「粘住」构成。其分词 inhaerens 给出形容词，英语十七世纪引入。同一词根还产生 adhere 与 hesitate。

items.en: Haerere meant to stick, to cling or to be stuck fast, and it could describe both glue and a stalled mind.
items.cn: haerere 意为粘住、附着或卡住不动，既能形容胶，也能形容卡住的思路。

items.en: With in- 'in', inhaerere meant to stick inside something, and it described qualities that cling to a subject.
items.cn: 加 in-「在内」，inhaerere 意为粘在内部，用来描述附着于主体的性质。

items.en: The participle inhaerens named what inheres, and philosophy used it for properties that belong to a substance.
items.cn: 分词 inhaerens 命名「内居的东西」，哲学用它指属于实体的属性。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in theology and natural philosophy before it became an everyday word.
items.cn: 英语在神学与自然哲学中先采用这个形容词，之后才成为日常用词。

items.en: Law uses inherent for powers and rights attached to an office, not created by a separate grant.
items.cn: 法律用这个词指附着于职位的权力与权利，而非由另一次授予创造。

items.en: Inherent stresses the attachment to a subject; intrinsic stresses what lies within a thing's own nature, apart from anything external.
items.cn: inherent 强调「附着于主体」；intrinsic 强调「属于事物自身本质内部、与外来因素无关」。

note.en: The first group shares the clinging stem; the second group holds the words most often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组共享「粘住」词干；第二组列出最容易被它与混淆的几个词。

entries.definition: To exist as a permanent quality in something; the verb behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 作为永久性质存在于某物之中；是形容词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The state of existing inside something as a quality; a formal philosophical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 作为性质存在于某物内部的状态；正式的哲学名词。

entries.definition: By its own nature; it marks a judgement about what cannot be changed.
entries.definitionCN: 就其本性而言；标出「无法改变」这一判断。

entries.definition: Sticking to a surface, or a person who supports a cause; it adds the idea of attaching from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 附着在表面上，或指拥护某个主张的人；多了「从外部贴上」之意。

entries.definition: Belonging to a thing's own inner nature, measured without reference to anything outside; it stresses the inside rather than the attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物自身的内在本质，不参照外部来量度；强调「内部」而非「附着」。

entries.definition: Present from birth, used mainly of living things and abilities; it marks origin in time rather than inseparability.
entries.definitionCN: 出生时即有，主要用于生物与能力；标出时间上的来源，而非不可分离。

entries.definition: Belonging to the essence, so that without it the thing would not be what it is; stronger than mere attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本质，缺了它事物就不成其为该物；比单纯「附着」更强。

entries.definition: Included as part of a product's design; the everyday compound for qualities installed rather than grown.
entries.definitionCN: 作为产品设计的一部分内置；是日常复合词，指装进去而非长出来的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'in' and the root means 'stick': inherent is stuck inside and will not come out.
normal.cn: 前缀是「在内」，词根是「粘」：固有的就是粘在里面取不出来。

normal.en: The family runs inhere, inherence, inherently and adherent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括固有、固有性、固有地、附着的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark risk and defect: inherent risk, inherent weakness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出风险与缺陷：固有风险、内在缺陷。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark law and logic: inherent right, inherent contradiction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律与逻辑：固有权利、内在矛盾。

normal.en: Its nearest rival is intrinsic: inherent clings to a subject, intrinsic lies in its own nature.
normal.cn: 最接近的对手是 intrinsic：前者附着于主体，后者属于自身本质。

abstract.en: Picture moss growing inside a crack that no knife can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象青苔长在刀也够不到的裂缝里。

abstract.en: Picture a bell whose hum is part of its metal, not the air.
abstract.cn: 想象钟的余音来自金属本身，而不是空气。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that exists in the game itself, not on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则存在于游戏本身，而不是贴在墙上。

examples.en: There is an inherent danger in climbing without a rope.
examples.cn: 徒手攀爬存在固有危险。

examples.en: The design has an inherent flaw that no software patch can fix.
examples.cn: 这个设计存在任何补丁都修不好的内在缺陷。

examples.en: Patience is inherent in good teaching, not added later.
examples.cn: 耐心是好教学本身固有的，而不是后来添上的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印海里」——像印在海里一样去不掉，就是固有

root: 拉丁 haerere「粘住」→ inhaerere「粘在里面」→ 分词 inhaerens → 英语 inherent；同根词 adhere、hesitate、coherent。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a quality stuck inside its owner: in matter, in a person, in a meaning, in a practice, in an office, in logic or in a body's defences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「粘在所有者内部」的性质：在材料里、在人身上、在词义里、在实践里、在职位里、在逻辑里，或在身体的防御里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quality lodged inside a substance, impossible to peel off without destroying it.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡在物质内部的一种性质，剥下来就会毁掉该物。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL SIDE: what belongs to a substance or alloy rather than to its treatment.
branches.cn: 材料一面：属于物质或合金本身，而非加工带来的。

branches.en: THE PERSONAL SIDE: a trait present from birth.
branches.cn: 个人一面：出生时即有的特质。

branches.en: THE LINGUISTIC SIDE: a suggestion carried inside a word's meaning.
branches.cn: 语言一面：藏在词义里的暗示。

branches.en: THE BUILT-IN BURDEN: a risk tied to the practice, and a contradiction following from the definition.
branches.cn: 自带负担：与实践绑在一起的风险，以及由定义推出的矛盾。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL SIDE: powers held by an office, and defences present from the start.
branches.cn: 建制一面：职位自带的权利，以及从一开始就有的防御。

intro.en: Inherent is Latin in- 'in' plus haerere 'to stick', with the present participle ending -ens and the English adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: inherent 由拉丁 in-「在内」与 haerere「粘住」构成，带现在分词词尾 -ens 与英语形容词词尾 -ent。

latinIntro.en: Haerere 'to stick' gives inhaerere 'to stick in'; its participle inhaerens gives the adjective, and the same root gives adhere and hesitate.
latinIntro.cn: haerere「粘住」给出 inhaerere「粘在里面」；其分词 inhaerens 给出形容词，同一词根还给出 adhere 与 hesitate。

items.example: The verb states the relation plainly.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词平实地陈述这种关系。

items.example: The adverb marks judgement by nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词标出「就本性而言」的判断。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of clinging.

sceneCN: 这里指由自身构造决定的性质（第 1 个义项：修饰形容词，指本质属性）；句意为果核的苦味本质上来自化学构造，与烹饪方式无关。

senses.title: By its own nature
senses.definition: in a way that belongs to the essential nature of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 以属于某物本质的方式
senses.example: The material is inherently brittle at low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料在低温下本身就很脆。
senses.why: Modifying an adjective, it says the property comes from what the thing is, not from how it is used.
senses.whyCN: 修饰形容词时，它说明这一性质来自事物本身，而不是来自它的用法。

senses.title: Not by circumstance
senses.definition: used to contrast an internal cause with external conditions
senses.definitionCN: 用来把内部原因与外部条件形成对照
senses.example: The conflict was inherently structural rather than personal.
senses.exampleCN: 这场冲突本质上是结构性的，而不是个人恩怨。
senses.why: The word shifts the explanation from situation to design, and the contrast with rather than is typical.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把解释从处境移到构造上，与「而不是」搭配的对照很典型。

senses.title: Inherently linked
senses.definition: used of two things whose connection cannot be separated
senses.definitionCN: 用于两者之间无法分离的联系
senses.example: Freedom of speech is inherently linked to responsibility.
senses.exampleCN: 言论自由与责任天然相连。
senses.why: In this fixed pattern the adverb marks an inseparable relation, close to by definition.
senses.whyCN: 在这一固定搭配里，副词标记不可分离的关系，接近「按定义就是如此」。

senses.title: No system is inherently safe
senses.definition: used with a negative to deny that a property is guaranteed by the thing alone
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，否认某一性质仅凭事物本身就能保证
senses.example: No encryption method is inherently secure against every attack.
senses.exampleCN: 没有哪种加密方法本身就足以抵御一切攻击。
senses.why: Under negation the word attacks a naive assumption: the thing may become safe, but not by nature alone.
senses.whyCN: 在否定句中它针对一种天真假设：事物可以变安全，但不是单靠本性。

senses.title: Inherently more stable
senses.titleCN: 比较句中的结构性优势
senses.definition: used before a comparative to claim that an advantage comes from design
senses.definitionCN: 放在比较级前，主张优势来自结构本身
senses.example: The arched form is inherently more stable than a flat one.
senses.exampleCN: 拱形结构本身就比平直结构更稳定。
senses.why: With a comparative, the word argues that the difference is built into the structure, not added later.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它主张差别已写进结构中，而不是后来附加的。

senses.title: Inherently ambiguous
senses.titleCN: 技术与学术中的固有难题
senses.definition: in technical or academic prose, marking a difficulty that cannot be engineered away
senses.definitionCN: 在技术或学术散文中，标记无法靠工程手段消除的困难
senses.example: Translation is inherently ambiguous when two languages divide the world differently.
senses.exampleCN: 当两种语言对世界的划分不同时，翻译本身就有歧义。
senses.why: The register presents the difficulty as a property of the task, which limits what any method can promise.
senses.whyCN: 这一语域把困难说成任务本身的属性，从而限制任何方法能承诺的范围。

senses.title: Inherently valuable
senses.definition: used in ethics to say that value belongs to a thing, not to its usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 在伦理讨论中指价值属于事物本身，而不属于它的用处
senses.example: The forest is inherently valuable, not merely a store of timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林本身就有价值，不只是木材的储备。
senses.why: Ethical writing uses the word to separate worth in itself from instrumental worth.
senses.whyCN: 伦理写作借它把「自身的价值」与「作为工具的价值」分开。

senses.title: Inherently limited
senses.definition: used of a capacity that cannot exceed what the design allows
senses.definitionCN: 用于无法超出设计所允许范围的能力
senses.example: Human memory is inherently limited in the number of items it can hold.
senses.exampleCN: 人的记忆在能容纳的条目数量上本身就有上限。
senses.why: The word describes a ceiling set by the nature of the system, often with a hint of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述由系统本性设定的上限，常带一点无奈的接受。

intro.en: Inherently comes from the Latin verb for sticking fast inside, through its participle and adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「牢牢粘在内部」的动词，经分词与形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb haerere means to stick, cling or be fixed in place.
items.cn: 动词意为「粘住、附着、固定在某处」。

items.en: The prefix in-, meaning in, plus haerere gives inhaerere, to stick fast inside something.
items.cn: 表示「在内」的前缀与「粘住」合成「牢牢附着于某物之内」。

items.en: The present participle inhaerens, sticking in, becomes the source of the adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词意为「附着于内的」，成为形容词的来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin inheren(t)- supplies the adjective stem used in philosophy and law.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语提供哲学与法学使用的形容词词干。

items.en: English inherent appears in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十六世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and spreads into technical and ethical argument.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，并扩展到技术与伦理讨论。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin sticking-root, including words built with other prefixes; the second group contrasts inherent belonging with value or quality viewed in itself.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「粘附」词根，包括带其他前缀的同族词；第二组对照「固有属性」与「就本身而言」的价值或性质。

entries.definition: To exist as a permanent quality in something.
entries.definitionCN: 作为恒久性质存在于某物之中。

entries.definition: The state of existing as part of a thing's nature.
entries.definitionCN: 作为事物本性的一部分而存在的状态。

entries.definition: Sticking to a surface or to a person or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于表面，或追随某人、某项事业。

entries.definition: Sticking together logically; consistent and clear.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑上彼此粘合；连贯而清晰。

entries.definition: In itself, considered apart from its use or setting; the emphasis falls on the thing viewed alone.
entries.definitionCN: 就本身而言，撇开用途与处境；重心在单独看待该事物。

entries.definition: From birth or from the earliest nature, often of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来地，多用于生物。

entries.definition: Because of the character a thing or person has.
entries.definitionCN: 由于事物或人本身的性格、特性。

entries.definition: At the deepest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 在最深层、最基础层面上。

entries.definition: In its essential respects, when everything secondary is set aside.
entries.definitionCN: 就本质方面而言，撇开一切次要因素。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real sticking-root and the real patterns of blame, negation and technical limits.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「粘附」词根，以及归因、否定与技术限度中的真实搭配。

normal.en: The root means to stick fast, so an inherent quality is glued into the thing and cannot be peeled off.
normal.cn: 词根意为「牢牢粘住」，所以固有属性是粘进事物内部、揭不下来的。

normal.en: With rather than it moves the explanation away from people and situations.
normal.cn: 与「而不是」连用时，它把解释从人和处境上移开。

normal.en: No system is inherently safe is a warning, not a compliment.
normal.cn: 「没有系统本身就安全」是一句警告，不是称赞。

normal.en: Before a comparative it says the advantage was designed in, not added on.
normal.cn: 放在比较级前，它说优势是设计进去的，不是后加的。

normal.en: Ethics uses it to say a thing matters for what it is, not for what it sells.
normal.cn: 伦理学用它说明某物因其本身而重要，而不是因其售价。

abstract.en: An inherent property is the grain in the wood that no surface polish can change.
abstract.cn: 固有属性就是木头里的纹理，表面打磨改变不了它。

abstract.en: Blaming a design instead of a person is a way of saying the outcome was already inside the plan.
abstract.cn: 把责任归于设计而非个人，等于说结果早已藏在方案里。

abstract.en: To call a limit inherent is to stop promising that more effort will remove it.
abstract.cn: 把限度说成固有，就是不再承诺更多努力能把它消除。

examples.en: The task is inherently social, since it cannot be done without others.
examples.cn: 这项任务本质上是社会性的，因为没有他人就无法完成。

examples.en: Some risk is inherently attached to every surgical procedure.
examples.cn: 每台手术都固有地带有一定风险。

examples.en: The method is inherently slow but extremely accurate.
examples.cn: 这种方法本身很慢，却极为精确。

root: 拉丁语动词「粘住」加表示「在内」的前缀，构成「牢牢附着于内」的分词与形容词；英语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate essential nature, contrast with circumstance, inseparable linking, negated guarantees, structural comparison, built-in difficulty, value in itself, and design-imposed limits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理本质属性、与外部条件的对照、不可分离的联系、被否定的保证、结构性比较、固有难题、自身价值，以及设计带来的限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the grain inside a block of wood, invisible on the surface but running through the whole material.
core.cn: 核心意象：木块内部的纹理，表面看不见却贯穿整块材料。

branches.en: THE NATURE: a property that comes from what the thing is.
branches.cn: 本性：来自事物之所以为该物的性质。

branches.en: THE INNER CAUSE: the explanation lies in design, not circumstance.
branches.cn: 内部原因：解释落在构造上，而非处境上。

branches.en: THE GLUE: a connection that cannot be separated.
branches.cn: 粘合：无法分离的联系。

branches.en: THE DENIED GUARANTEE AND THE BUILT-IN EDGE: what nature does not promise, and what it does provide.
branches.cn: 被否认的保证与内置优势：本性不承诺什么，又确实提供什么。

branches.en: THE UNAVOIDABLE SHAPE: difficulty, value and limits that belong to the thing itself.
branches.cn: 无法回避的形态：属于事物本身的困难、价值与限度。

intro.en: Inherently is a Latin in-prefix, a Latin sticking-root and participle ending, plus an English adverb suffix. The same root also builds coherent and adherent.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「在内」前缀、「粘附」词根与分词词尾，再加英语副词后缀构成；同一词根还构成「连贯的」与「附着的」。

latinIntro.en: The root haerere is about clinging; the prefix decides whether the clinging is inward, together or toward something.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「粘住」；前缀决定这种粘附是向内、彼此相合，还是朝向某物。

items.example: The prefix locates the sticking inside the thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「粘附」定位在事物内部。

items.example: The verb gives the physical image of glue.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「胶水粘住」的具体意象。

items.example: The compound verb makes the attachment internal.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把这种附着变成内部的。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into a description of a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成对事物的描述。

items.example: The participle supplies the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供形容词词干。

items.example: A different prefix gives the English word adherent.
items.exampleCN: 换一个前缀就得到英语的「附着的」。

items.example: The same root with a together-prefix gives coherent.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根配上「共同」前缀，得到「连贯的」。

items.example: The suffix turns inherent into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The noun names the state that the adverb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名副词所描述的状态。
