definition_zh: 继承（财产、地位或特征）；接手（遗留的问题）
definition_en: to receive money, property, or qualities from someone who has died or come before you
core_image: 老人留下的钥匙和账簿被交到下一代手里
scene: 祖父去世后，律师在书房里宣读遗嘱。She inherited the old farmhouse and all the land around it.
sceneCN: 这里 inherit 是「继承财产」（第 1 个义项：从去世的人那里接受钱财或产业）；句意为她继承了那座旧农舍以及周围所有土地。图中可辨识物件：遗嘱、钥匙、旧账簿。

pos.zh: 动词：继承；接手；遗传获得

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「遗产；继承」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「继承人」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「可继承的」
由本词加否定前缀构成，义为「剥夺继承权」

senses.title: To receive property from the dead
senses.definition: to receive money, property, or a title from someone after that person has died
senses.definitionCN: 在某人身故后接受其钱财、产业或头衔
senses.example: She inherited the house from her aunt.
senses.exampleCN: 她从姑妈那里继承了这所房子。
senses.why: In- "in" plus heres "heir" gave inhereditare, to put someone in the position of an heir.
senses.whyCN: in-「进入」加 heres「继承人」构成 inhereditare，意为把人放进继承人的位置。

senses.title: To take over a legacy of problems
senses.definition: to receive a situation, problem, or duty that someone else has left behind
senses.definitionCN: 接受别人留下的局面、问题或职责
senses.example: The new mayor inherited a city deep in debt.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长接手了一座负债累累的城市。
senses.why: What is passed down is not always wealth; an office or a mess can be handed over in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 传下来的不总是财富；职位或一团乱局也能以同样的方式移交。

senses.title: To get a quality through genes
senses.definition: to receive a physical or personal quality from one's parents or ancestors through genes
senses.definitionCN: 通过基因从父母或祖先那里获得身体或性格特征
senses.example: He inherited his mother's quick temper.
senses.exampleCN: 他遗传了母亲的急性子。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the legal image: parents hand down traits as families hand down land.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了法律上的意象：父母传下特征，正如家族传下土地。

intro.en: Inherit is a legal Latin word whose heir has become the everyday word for anything handed down.
intro.cn: inherit 本是一个法律拉丁词，其中的「继承人」如今成了泛指一切传承的日常语汇。

items.en: Heres meant "heir", a person who steps into another's property and standing.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」，指接替他人财产与地位的人。

items.en: Inhereditare, "to make an heir", built in- onto heres and was used of transferring an estate.
items.cn: inhereditare 意为「使成为继承人」，由 in- 加 heres 构成，用于转移产业。

items.en: Old French enheriter, "to make heir, to put in possession", shortened the form on its way to English.
items.cn: 古法语 enheriter 意为「立为继承人、使其占有」，在传入英语时形式缩短。

items.en: English took inherit in the fourteenth century, first in law, then in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入 inherit，先用于法律，后进入日常语言。

items.en: Since the nineteenth century it also covers traits passed through genes, not just property.
items.cn: 十九世纪以后，它也涵盖经基因传下的特征，而不只是财产。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the heir root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of receiving from someone else.
note.cn: 形近组保留「继承人」词根；近义组收其他表示「从他人处获得」的动词。

entries.definition: What is inherited, whether money or a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗产、遗传」，指被继承之物。

entries.definition: The person who inherits property or a title.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「继承人」，即继承财产或头衔的人。

entries.definition: The traditions and buildings a society passes down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗产、传统」，指社会传下的传统与建筑。

entries.definition: To take over an office or title after another person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「继任」，多指接替职位或头衔。

entries.definition: To get something given to you, without the idea of a death.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收到」，不含继承的意味。

entries.definition: To gain something by your own effort or purchase.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，强调靠自己努力或购买。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real heir root and the phrases the word actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「继承人」词根，以及这个词实际使用的搭配。

normal.en: Heres is heir: to inherit is to be put in the heir's place.
normal.cn: heres 就是「继承人」：inherit 就是被放进继承人位置。

normal.en: The same root gives heir, heritage and inheritance.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 heir、heritage、inheritance。

normal.en: You inherit money from a person, but you inherit a problem from a situation.
normal.cn: 钱是从人那里 inherit 来的，问题是从局面那里 inherit 来的。

normal.en: An inherited disease comes through the genes, not through a will.
normal.cn: inherited disease 是通过基因而非遗嘱得来的。

normal.en: A new manager often inherits the mistakes of the old one.
normal.cn: 新经理常常要接手前任犯下的错误。

abstract.en: Picture a key passed from an old hand to a young one: the door opens for the new owner.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙从老人的手交到年轻人的手里：门为新主人打开。

abstract.en: Inheritance is time travelling forward: the past arrives in the present as property, habit or illness.
abstract.cn: 继承是时间向前旅行：过去以财产、习惯或疾病的形式抵达现在。

abstract.en: You choose what to keep and what to change, but you cannot choose what you were handed.
abstract.cn: 你可以选择保留什么、改变什么，却无法选择自己被交到手里的东西。

examples.en: He inherited a small workshop from his father.
examples.cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一间小作坊。

examples.en: Children often inherit the habits of their parents.
examples.cn: 孩子常会遗传父母的习惯。

examples.en: The committee inherited an unfinished project.
examples.cn: 委员会接手了一个没做完的项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因何丽特」——因何丽特得了遗产？因为她继承了老屋

root: 拉丁语 heres「继承人」加上 in- 构成 inhereditare「使成为继承人」，经古法语 enheriter 传入英语作 inherit；同根词有 heir、heritage、inheritance、heredity。十九世纪起又用于遗传学。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one image of handover: property after a death, a situation left by a predecessor, and traits passed through genes.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用一个「移交」意象：身后的财产、前任留下的局面，以及经基因传下的特征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key and an account book pass from an old hand to a young one.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙与账簿从老人的手交到年轻人手里。

branches.en: THE WILL: property passes at death, and the law records who receives it.
branches.cn: 遗嘱这条线：财产在身故时转移，法律记录由谁接受。

branches.en: THE TITLE: names and offices are inherited as readily as land.
branches.cn: 头衔这条线：姓氏与职位和土地一样可以被继承。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a successor inherits whatever the predecessor left, good or bad.
branches.cn: 职位这条线：继任者接手前任留下的一切，无论好坏。

branches.en: THE BODY: genes hand down traits as families hand down land.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：基因传下特征，正如家族传下土地。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in every sense something arrives from the past and must be carried on.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项里都有东西从过去抵达，并须被延续。

intro.en: Inherit is a Latin prefix plus the Latin word for heir, reshaped in Old French and English.
intro.cn: inherit 是拉丁语前缀加拉丁语「继承人」一词，经古法语与英语改写而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres and inhereditare are recorded; the related heredity shows the same root in modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres 与 inhereditare 均有记录，现代英语的 heredity 显示同一词根。

definition_zh: 继承（物）；遗产；遗传；（文化）传承；继承权
definition_en: property or a right received from someone who has died, or the transmission of traits and traditions from one generation to the next

scene: 老宅的钥匙和地契被装进同一个木匣，交到下一代手里。The eldest daughter received the farm as her inheritance.
sceneCN: 这里 inheritance 指「从去世的亲人那里接下的财产」（第 1 个义项：继承所得的财物）；句意为长女把这座农场作为遗产接了下来。可辨识物件：木匣、黄铜钥匙、地契、裂开的封蜡。

senses.title: Property received after a death
senses.titleCN: 从逝者那里接下的财产
senses.definition: money or property passed to an heir after someone dies
senses.definitionCN: 某人去世后传给继承人的钱财或财产
senses.example: She used her inheritance to buy the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 她用继承来的钱买下了那间作坊。
senses.why: The word names what is handed over at death, so the first sense is the concrete estate rather than the act of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指在死亡时被交出的东西，因此第一个义项是具体的遗产，而不是领取的动作。

senses.title: The act or right of inheriting
senses.definition: the legal act or right by which an heir receives an estate
senses.definitionCN: 继承人取得遗产的法定行为或权利
senses.example: The inheritance of the land was disputed for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地的继承权争了多年。
senses.why: Because the noun covers both the thing and the legal relation, English can speak of an inheritance and of the right of inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词同时涵盖财物与法律关系，英语既能说「一份遗产」，也能说「继承权」。

senses.title: Genetic transmission
senses.definition: the passing of traits from parents to offspring through genes
senses.definitionCN: 性状经基因由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Eye colour shows a simple pattern of inheritance.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛颜色呈现出简单的遗传模式。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century biology borrowed the legal word because traits seemed to be handed down like property.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的生物学借用了这个法律词，因为性状看起来像财产一样被传下去。

senses.title: Cultural heritage
senses.definition: the traditions, language or art received from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 从更早世代接下的传统、语言或艺术
senses.example: The city claims the inheritance of three empires.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市自称承袭了三个帝国的遗产。
senses.why: The legal frame widened to anything received from the past, so a city can inherit an empire's habits of building.
senses.whyCN: 法律框架被拓宽到任何从过去接下的东西，因此一座城市可以继承一个帝国的建造习惯。

senses.title: A burden or condition passed on
senses.titleCN: 一并接下的负担或状况
senses.definition: a debt, problem or condition that comes with what is received
senses.definitionCN: 随所得之物一起到来的债务、问题或状况
senses.example: He carries an inheritance of debt from the previous owner.
senses.exampleCN: 他背上了前任业主留下的一身债务。
senses.why: What is inherited is not always a gift; the word can name the liabilities that arrive with the property.
senses.whyCN: 被继承的不总是礼物；这个词也能指随财产一起到来的负担。

senses.title: Class inheritance in computing
senses.definition: the mechanism by which one class or module takes properties from a parent
senses.definitionCN: 一个类或模块从父级取得属性的机制
senses.example: Class inheritance lets one module reuse another's methods.
senses.exampleCN: 类继承让一个模块可以复用另一个模块的方法。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the family metaphor: a child class receives behaviour from its parent, just as an heir receives property.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用了家庭隐喻：子类从父类取得行为，正如继承人取得财产。

senses.title: Inheritance tax and legal thresholds
senses.definition: the tax charged on an estate before or after it passes to heirs
senses.definitionCN: 遗产传给继承人之前或之后所征的税
senses.example: Inheritance tax applies above a fixed threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产税适用于超过固定起征点的部分。
senses.why: Once the state began taxing transfers at death, the noun became fixed in the compound inheritance tax.
senses.whyCN: 当国家开始对死亡时的财产转移征税后，这个名词就固定于遗产税这一复合词中。

senses.title: A legacy of consequences
senses.definition: the lasting effects that one period or action leaves to those who follow
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期或行动留给后来者的持久影响
senses.example: The reform left an inheritance of distrust.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革留下了一份不信任的遗产。
senses.why: The metaphor treats consequences as an estate: later people receive them whether they want them or not.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把后果当作一份产业：后来者不管愿不愿意都得接收。

intro.en: Inheritance comes from Anglo-French enheritance, from enheriter 'to make an heir', from Late Latin inhereditare, built on heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: inheritance 来自盎格鲁-法语 enheritance，源自动词 enheriter「立为继承人」，再上溯为晚期拉丁 inhereditare，其词干是 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; suggestions linking it to other Indo-European words are hypotheses, and any PIE form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；把它与其他印欧语词联系起来的说法只是假说，凡为其给出的原始印欧语形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Hereditas 'inheritance, heirship' and hereditarius 'of an heir' were formed on the hered- stem.
items.cn: hereditas「继承、继承权」与 hereditarius「继承人的」都建立在 hered- 词干上。

items.en: In- 'in, into' plus hereditare 'to inherit' gave inhereditare 'to appoint as heir'.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 hereditare「继承」构成 inhereditare「立为继承人」。

items.en: Enheriter and its noun enheritance reached English in the fourteenth century; legal use came first, and the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: enheriter 及其名词 enheritance 在 14 世纪进入英语；法律用法最先出现，确切的最早书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word was extended to the transmission of traits, alongside the new science of heredity.
items.cn: 19 世纪，随着遗传学兴起，这个词被扩展到性状传递。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): first dates for the biological sense are approximate, and the pre-Latin origin of heres remains uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：生物学义项的首见年代只是约数，heres 在拉丁语之前的来源仍不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same hered- stem or that merely look similar; group two holds the legal and everyday words for what is left to heirs.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hered- 词干或仅形近的词；第二组是法律与日常语境中表示「留给继承人的东西」的近义词。

entries.tag: same root what is handed down
entries.definition: The same Latin hered- stem, but heritage usually names cultural or family possessions rather than a legal share.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁 hered- 词干，但 heritage 通常指文化或家族传承物，而非法定份额。

entries.definition: The biological transmission of traits, not the property received; the two words split in the nineteenth century.
entries.definitionCN: 指性状的生物传递，而非所收财产；两个词在 19 世纪分化。

entries.definition: The person who receives, not the thing received; the suffix -or marks the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指接收的人，而非所收之物；后缀 -or 标记施事者。

entries.definition: From inhaerere 'to stick in', not heres: the state of being inherent or built into something. The resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 inhaerere「黏附于内」，并非 heres：指内在于某物的状态。相似只是偶然。

entries.definition: A specific gift left in a will; inheritance can also mean the whole estate or the right to it.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱中留下的具体馈赠；inheritance 还可指全部遗产或继承权。

entries.definition: Property given by a will, usually personal items; narrower and more legal than inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱赠予的财产，通常为个人物品；比 inheritance 更窄、更法律化。

entries.definition: The total property a person leaves, before it is divided among heirs.
entries.definitionCN: 某人留下的全部财产，在分配给继承人之前。

entries.definition: Money or property given to an institution, often to produce income; it stresses the lasting gift rather than the heir.
entries.definitionCN: 捐给机构的钱或财产，常用来产生收益；强调持续的馈赠而非继承人。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'in' + heres 'heir': being put into the heir's place.
normal.cn: in-「进入」+ heres「继承人」：被放进继承人的位置。

normal.en: The family runs inherit, inheritance, inheritor, inheritable, hereditary and heredity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 inherit、inheritance、inheritor、inheritable、hereditary 与 heredity。

normal.en: Legal use came first; the biological use is a nineteenth-century extension.
normal.cn: 法律用法最先出现，生物学用法是 19 世纪的扩展。

normal.en: In computing, inheritance means a subclass takes methods from its parent.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，inheritance 指子类从父类取得方法。

abstract.en: Picture a house key passed from hand to hand until the first hand is forgotten.
abstract.cn: 想象一把房门钥匙被一双手传一双手，直到最初那双手被遗忘。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card whose stains are inherited along with the recipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食谱卡，油渍和做法一起被继承下来。

abstract.en: Picture a debt that arrives with the furniture and has no invoice.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债务随家具一起到来，却没有账单。

examples.en: The inheritance was divided equally among the four children.
examples.cn: 遗产在四个孩子之间平均分配。

examples.en: Researchers traced the inheritance of the trait across five generations.
examples.cn: 研究者追踪了这一性状在五代人中的遗传。

examples.en: Class inheritance reduced the amount of code the team had to write.
examples.cn: 类继承减少了团队需要编写的代码量。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: a box passes at death and becomes property, a right, a biological trait, a culture, a burden, a piece of code, a tax and finally a set of consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：一只匣子在死亡时被递出，成为财产、权利、生物性状、文化、负担、代码、税，最后成为一整套后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden box of keys and deeds passing from one hand to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着钥匙与地契的木匣，从一双手递到另一双手。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND RIGHT: the estate itself and the legal power to receive it.
branches.cn: 财产与权利：遗产本身，以及取得它的法定资格。

branches.en: WHAT IS TRANSMITTED: a trait can arrive like property, and so can a debt.
branches.cn: 被传递之物：性状可以像财产一样到来，债务也可以。

branches.en: CULTURE: buildings, language and habits are received from earlier generations.
branches.cn: 文化：建筑、语言与习惯从更早世代接下。

branches.en: COMPUTING: a child class receives behaviour from its parent class.
branches.cn: 计算机：子类从父类取得行为。

branches.en: TAX AND CONSEQUENCE: the state takes a share, and later people receive the effects.
branches.cn: 税与后果：国家取走一份，后来者接收影响。

intro.en: Inheritance is built from a Latin prefix and the hered- stem, and the same pieces form a large legal and biological family.
intro.cn: inheritance 由拉丁前缀与 hered- 词干构成，这些成分组成了一个庞大的法律与生物词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, inherit and inheritance; in- adds the sense of entering a position.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、inherit 与 inheritance；in- 增添「进入某一位置」的意思。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.

items.meaning: to inherit; to leave as an inheritance

items.exampleCN: hereditare 把「继承人」变成了动作。

items.example: The Late Latin verb added the legal act of naming an heir.
items.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁动词增添了指定继承人的法律动作。

items.meaning: the estate or the act of receiving it

definition_zh: 抑制；阻止；约束；禁止；使（生物或化学反应）受抑制
definition_en: to hold something back, slow it down or keep it from acting freely
core_image: 一只手紧紧按住正在弹开的阀门手柄，压力表指针停在原位不再上冲
scene: 实验台上，学生往培养皿里滴入一滴药剂，菌落的扩散立刻停在划好的圈内。A single dose can inhibit the growth of the bacteria for hours.
sceneCN: 这里指用药剂阻止细菌继续生长（第 1 个义项：抑制生物或化学过程）；句意为一次给药就能让这些细菌的生长停止数小时。

pos.zh: 抑制；阻止；约束；禁止

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示「行为、状态」的名词尾构成，义为「抑制；拘谨」
由动词加表示「施动者」的名词尾构成，义为「抑制剂；抑制物」
由动词加表示「起……作用的」形容词尾构成，义为「抑制性的」
由动词加已然词尾构成，义为「受抑制的；拘谨的」
由动词加表示「倾向于」的形容词尾构成，义为「有抑制作用的」
由表示「不」的前缀加已然形容词构成，义为「不受约束的；放纵的」

senses.title: Slow a living or chemical process
senses.definition: to reduce the rate or extent of a biological or chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 降低生物或化学过程的速度或程度
senses.example: Cold temperatures inhibit the growth of most moulds.
senses.exampleCN: 低温会抑制大多数霉菌的生长。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to hold in, and a process that is held in simply runs slower.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「按住、拦住」，被按住的过程自然就跑得慢了。

senses.title: Hold a person back
senses.definition: to make a person less willing or less able to act freely
senses.definitionCN: 使人不愿或不能自由行动
senses.example: Fear of criticism inhibited her from speaking at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 对批评的畏惧使她不敢在会上发言。
senses.why: The same holding image applies to a person: something inside keeps the action from coming out.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「按住」的意象也用在人身上：心里有东西把行动压了回去。

senses.title: Block an enzyme or reaction
senses.definition: to interfere with a molecule or reaction so that it cannot proceed normally
senses.definitionCN: 干扰分子或反应，使其无法正常进行
senses.example: The drug inhibits an enzyme that the virus needs to copy itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药抑制病毒复制自身所需的一种酶。
senses.why: Biochemistry borrowed the word for anything that stops a molecular step, since stopping is a form of holding back.
senses.whyCN: 生物化学借这个词指任何阻断分子步骤的东西，因为阻断就是一种按住。

senses.title: Forbid by authority
senses.definition: to forbid something officially, especially by a church or a legal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由教会或法律权威正式禁止某事
senses.example: The old rule inhibited the sale of land to outsiders.
senses.exampleCN: 旧规定禁止把土地卖给外来者。
senses.why: Church law used the word for a formal ban, and the meaning of a public prohibition grew from that usage.
senses.whyCN: 教会法用这个词表示正式禁令，公开禁止的含义就是从这种用法长出来的。

senses.title: Dampen growth or development
senses.definition: to keep an economy, industry or activity from expanding as it otherwise would
senses.definitionCN: 使经济、行业或活动无法按原本的速度扩张
senses.example: High taxes may inhibit small firms from hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 高税收可能抑制小企业招人。
senses.why: An expanding thing is imagined as a force pushing outward, and inhibiting is the hand that pushes back.
senses.whyCN: 扩张的事物被想象成向外推的力量，而抑制就是把它推回去的那只手。

senses.title: Suppress a nerve signal
senses.definition: to reduce or block the transmission of a signal along a nerve or circuit
senses.definitionCN: 减弱或阻断沿神经或电路传递的信号
senses.example: This pathway inhibits the nerve that carries the pain signal.
senses.exampleCN: 这条通路会抑制传递疼痛信号的神经。
senses.why: In physiology the word names the braking side of the nervous system, the part that holds a signal down.
senses.whyCN: 在生理学里，这个词指神经系统中「刹车」的那一侧，也就是把信号按住的部分。

senses.title: Restrain an impulse or emotion
senses.definition: to keep an impulse or feeling from being expressed openly
senses.definitionCN: 使冲动或情绪不被公开表达出来
senses.example: He had learned to inhibit his anger in front of clients.
senses.exampleCN: 他学会了在客户面前克制自己的怒气。
senses.why: Social training is described as a restraint placed on feeling, which is the literal sense applied inward.
senses.whyCN: 社会训练被描述为对情绪施加的约束，这就是字面义转向内心的用法。

senses.title: Hold back investment or activity
senses.definition: to make investors or buyers unwilling to spend, so that activity falls
senses.definitionCN: 使投资者或买家不愿支出，从而使活动减少
senses.example: Uncertainty about the rules inhibited investment for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 规则不明朗抑制了投资长达两年。
senses.why: Money that is held back does not circulate, and the word covers that economic hesitation as well.
senses.whyCN: 被按住的钱不流通，这个词也覆盖这种经济上的迟疑。

intro.en: Inhibit comes from Latin inhibere, to hold in or keep back, built from in-, into, and habere, to hold. English first used it for official prohibitions, then for any restraining force, including chemical and neural ones.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 inhibere「按住、拦住」，由表示「向内」的前缀与表示「持有、握住」的词根构成。英语最初用它表示官方禁止，后来扩展到任何起约束作用的力量，包括化学与神经层面的抑制。

items.en: Habere meant to have or hold, and it stands behind a large family of English words about possession and restraint.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「有、握住」，英语中一大批表示持有与约束的词都出自它。

items.en: The prefix in- added the idea of direction inward, so the verb pictured a force holding something inside its own limits.
items.cn: 前缀给它加上「向内」的方向，于是这个动词画出的是把某物按在其限度之内的力。

items.en: The action noun named a keeping back or a prohibition, and it passed into English as inhibition.
items.cn: 动作名词表示「按住、禁止」，进入英语后成为「抑制」这一名词。

items.en: English took the verb through French and used it first for forbidding a person from acting; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入这个动词，最初用于禁止某人行动；确切的最早年代不确定。

items.en: A bishop could inhibit a cleric from exercising office, and the word carried that official weight for centuries.
items.cn: 主教可以禁止教士行使职务，这个词带着这种官方分量用了好几个世纪。

items.en: Physiology and chemistry adopted the word for any agent that slows a process, and that sense now dominates.
items.cn: 生理学与化学采用这个词指任何使过程变慢的因素，这一义项如今占主导。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root or merely looks similar; the second group gathers verbs of restraining and forbidding.
note.cn: 第一组或共享拉丁词根，或只是形近；第二组收集表示约束与禁止的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of restraining, and also for shyness that holds a person back.
entries.definitionCN: 指抑制行为，也指使人退缩的拘谨。

entries.definition: A substance or device that slows or blocks a process.
entries.definitionCN: 指使过程变慢或被阻断的物质或装置。

entries.definition: Held back from free expression; reserved in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指表达受压抑、举止拘谨的。

entries.definition: Free from restraint and showing feelings openly.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受约束、坦然表露情感的。

entries.definition: To show something publicly; it shares the hold root but the prefix points outward.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开展示；与抑制共享「握住」词根，但前缀指向外。

entries.definition: To live in a place; it looks close but belongs to the root for dwelling, not for holding.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住于某地；形近但属于「居住」词根，与「握住」无关。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something under control, often by physical or moral force.
entries.definitionCN: 指以体力或道德力量把某人某事控制住。

entries.definition: To stop something by force, or to keep a feeling from showing.
entries.definitionCN: 指以强力制止，或压住情绪不使其外露。

entries.definition: To make an action slower or harder without stopping it completely.
entries.definitionCN: 指使行动变慢或变难，但不完全停止。

entries.definition: To forbid something by law or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指依法律或规章禁止某事。

entries.definition: To keep something within limits, especially spending or growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指把开支或增长等控制在限度内。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the holding image, the real word family and the real scientific phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「按住」的意象、真实的同族词与真实的科学搭配。

normal.en: In- means in and habere means hold, so inhibit is literally to hold in.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向内」，词根意为「握住」，所以这个词字面上就是「往里按住」。

normal.en: An inhibitor is the thing that does the holding, and inhibition is the holding itself.
normal.cn: 抑制剂是执行按住的东西，抑制则是按住这个动作本身。

normal.en: A hand on a valve is the clearest picture: the flow is still there, only stopped.
normal.cn: 一只手按在阀门上是最清楚的画面：流仍在，只是被停住了。

normal.en: The word appears in enzyme inhibitor and immune inhibition, two fixed scientific phrases.
normal.cn: 这个词出现在「酶抑制剂」与「免疫抑制」两个固定的科学说法里。

normal.en: Inhibited behaviour is a person whose impulse has been held down before it reached the surface.
normal.cn: 拘谨的行为，就是冲动在浮出表面之前被按住了的人。

abstract.en: Restraint is not destruction: what is inhibited still exists, which is why a drug can stop a virus without killing it.
abstract.cn: 约束不等于毁灭：被抑制的东西仍然存在，所以药物能阻止病毒却不杀死它。

abstract.en: Every brake is a small inhibition, and a society is full of brakes that nobody calls by this name.
abstract.cn: 每一副刹车都是一次小小的抑制，社会里到处是没人用这个词称呼的刹车。

abstract.en: The word teaches that stopping and holding are the same gesture seen from two sides.
abstract.cn: 这个词说明，停止与按住是同一个手势的两面。

examples.en: Dry weather can inhibit the germination of these seeds.
examples.cn: 干燥天气会抑制这些种子发芽。

examples.en: The regulation was designed to inhibit speculation in the housing market.
examples.cn: 这项规定旨在抑制住房市场中的投机。

examples.en: A low dose inhibits the enzyme without damaging the surrounding tissue.
examples.cn: 低剂量会抑制这种酶，又不损伤周围组织。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因希比特」——把「因」由都按在「希」望的「比特」上：按住不让动，就是抑制、阻止

root: 拉丁语 inhibere「按住、拦住」← in-「向内」+ habere「持有、握住」；同根词有 exhibit「展出」（向外持）、inhibition「抑制」。英语十五世纪经法语引入，先用于教会与法律上的禁止，十九世纪后扩展到生理与化学的抑制。最早年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the laboratory to the courtroom: slowing a living process, holding a person back, blocking an enzyme, forbidding by authority, dampening growth, suppressing a nerve signal, restraining an impulse, and holding back investment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从实验室延伸到法庭：减慢生命过程、约束人的行动、阻断酶、以权力禁止、抑制增长、抑制神经信号、克制冲动、抑制投资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a firm hand presses a valve shut, and the pressure that was rising stops where it stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把阀门牢牢按住，原本上升的压力停在原处。

branches.en: THE SLOWED PROCESS: growth and expansion that are held to a lower rate.
branches.cn: 被减慢的过程：增长与扩张被压到更低的速率。

branches.en: THE RESTRAINED PERSON: action and feeling kept from coming out.
branches.cn: 被约束的人：行动与情绪被压住不外露。

branches.en: THE BLOCKED SIGNAL: an enzyme step or a nerve impulse that cannot pass.
branches.cn: 被阻断的信号：酶的步骤或神经冲动无法通过。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL BAN: a rule that forbids an act by authority.
branches.cn: 官方禁令：由权威以规则禁止某种行为。

branches.en: THE HELD-BACK MONEY: spending that waits instead of circulating.
branches.cn: 被按住的钱：支出停住而不流通。

intro.en: Inhibit is a Latin verb whose prefix and root still work separately in English words.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁动词，它的前缀与词根在英语其他词里仍然各自起作用。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies habere and inhibere; the family also includes the prefixed form exhibere, to hold out or show.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「持有」与「按住」两个词；同族还包括加外向前缀的「伸出、展示」。

items.example: It turns holding into holding in.
The root of many English words about possession.
items.exampleCN: 英语中许多表示拥有的词的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the English verb.
It became the English noun inhibition.
It forms inhibition from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词构成「抑制」这一名词。

items.example: It forms inhibitor for the substance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示物质的名词「抑制剂」。

items.example: It forms inhibitory for a kind of effect.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示作用性质的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective inhibited.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词「受抑制的」。

items.example: It forms uninhibited, the opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它构成反义词「不受约束的」。

items.example: It made exhibere, to hold out and show, the source of exhibit.
items.exampleCN: 它与同一词根构成「向外持」，即「展出」的来源。

senses.title: Inner shyness in company
senses.definition: a strong inner reluctance that makes a person hold back in social situations
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中使人退缩的强烈内在阻力
senses.example: Stage fright produced a strong inhibition in the young singer.
senses.exampleCN: 怯场让这位年轻歌手产生了强烈的抑制。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to hold in; psychology uses it for a brake applied from inside the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「扣住、收住」；心理学用它指人从内部踩下的刹车。

senses.title: Holding back an impulse
senses.definition: the checking of a desire, impulse or emotion before it becomes action
senses.definitionCN: 在欲望、冲动或情绪变成行动之前将其收住
senses.example: Years of strict training left him with an inhibition about asking for help.
senses.exampleCN: 多年严格训练让他对开口求助有一种克制。
senses.why: What is held in here is not a signal but a wish, and the holding is learned rather than mechanical.
senses.whyCN: 这里被收住的不是信号而是愿望，而且这种收住是学来的，不是机械的。

senses.title: Blocking a chemical reaction
senses.definition: the slowing or blocking of a chemical reaction, often by a substance that acts on an enzyme
senses.definitionCN: 对化学反应减速或阻断，常由作用于酶的物质造成
senses.example: Adding the compound caused inhibition of the enzyme within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该化合物后，酶在几分钟内受到抑制。
senses.why: Biochemistry kept the image of a hand held back and applied it to molecules that stop a catalyst.
senses.whyCN: 生物化学保留「被拉住的手」这一意象，把它用在对催化剂下手的大分子上。

senses.title: Slowing of growth or division
senses.definition: a reduction in the growth, division or reproduction of cells or organisms
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或生物体在生长、分裂或繁殖上的减弱
senses.example: The extract showed clear inhibition of bacterial growth in the dish.
senses.exampleCN: 该提取物在培养皿中明显抑制了细菌生长。
senses.why: Here the thing held back is a whole population of cells, not one reaction step.
senses.whyCN: 这里被拦住的是整个细胞群体，而不是某一个反应步骤。

senses.title: Quieting of a nerve signal
senses.definition: the dampening of neural activity so that a signal becomes weaker or stops
senses.definitionCN: 神经活动被压弱，使信号变弱或停止
senses.example: The drug produces inhibition of pain signals in the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物在脊髓中对疼痛信号产生抑制。
senses.why: The nervous system needs brakes as much as accelerators, and the word names those brakes.
senses.whyCN: 神经系统既需要加速器也需要刹车，这个词就指那些刹车。

senses.title: Suppression of a bodily function
senses.definition: the reduction or stopping of a secretion, reflex or organ function
senses.definitionCN: 对分泌、反射或器官功能的减弱或中止
senses.example: The treatment led to inhibition of acid secretion in the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 该治疗导致胃酸分泌受到抑制。
senses.why: Medicine applies the same noun to any function that is made to quiet down.
senses.whyCN: 医学把同一个名词用于任何被压下去的功能。

senses.title: A social taboo or constraint
senses.definition: a rule or custom that keeps people from saying or doing something
senses.definitionCN: 使人不敢说或不敢做的规则与习俗
senses.example: The old inhibition against discussing money has weakened among younger buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻消费者中，不谈钱的老禁忌已经减弱。
senses.why: The brake is no longer inside one mind but shared by a community.
senses.whyCN: 这时刹车不在某个人心里，而为一个群体所共有。

senses.title: Stiffness in performance
senses.definition: a lack of ease that makes a performance look guarded or forced
senses.definitionCN: 使表演显得拘束或做作的不自然状态
senses.example: The director asked the actors to drop their inhibition and move more freely.
senses.exampleCN: 导演要求演员放下拘束，动作更自由些。
senses.why: On stage the inner brake becomes visible: the body moves as if a strap were still on it.
senses.whyCN: 在舞台上，内心的刹车变得可见：身体动起来像还拴着带子。

intro.en: Inhibition comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold in, built from a prefix of inwardness and a root meaning to have or hold; psychology and biochemistry later gave it two technical lives.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「扣在里面」的动词，由表示「向内」的前缀与表示「持有、握住」的词根构成；心理学与生物化学后来给了它两条技术生命。

items.en: habere meant to have, to hold, to keep in one's hand.
items.cn: habere 意为「有、握住、拿在手里」。

items.en: in- carried the sense of in or against, so inhibere was to hold in, check or restrain.
items.cn: in- 带有「在内、对着」的意思，因此 inhibere 意为「扣住、制止、约束」。

items.en: The past participle named something already held back, and it became the stem of the English family.
items.cn: 过去分词指已被收住的东西，后来成为英语这一族词的词干。

items.en: The action noun inhibitio named the act of holding in or checking.
items.cn: 动作名词 inhibitio 命名「收住、制止」这一行为。

items.en: English first used the word for restraining a legal or physical action; the exact first date is not certain, but the Latin line is clear.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指对法律行为或身体动作的制止；具体首见年份不确定，但拉丁来源线索清楚。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word split into an inner brake of the mind and a chemical brake on enzymes and growth.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词分成两支：心智内部的刹车，以及作用于酶与生长的化学刹车。

note.en: The first group shares root or shape with inhibition; the second group names nearby brakes, and the note keeps their mechanisms apart.
note.cn: 第一组在词根或形音上与 inhibition 相近；第二组是邻近的「刹车」类词，说明中把它们的机制分开。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hold back, slow or forbid a process or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抑制、阻碍、使拘束」。

entries.definition: Describing a person who is held back and shows it in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一个人受拘束，并在行为上表现出来。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for a signal, drug or cell that suppresses activity.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指压抑活动的信号、药物或细胞。

entries.definition: A substance or agent that slows a reaction or a biological process.
entries.definitionCN: 指减缓反应或生物过程的物质或因子。

entries.definition: A public display; it uses the same holding root with ex-, to hold out, so the direction is opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开展览；同一「握住」词根配上表示「向外」的前缀，方向正好相反。

entries.definition: The act of living in a place; it looks close but comes from a verb for dwelling, not for holding in.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住在某地；形近，但来自表示「居住」的动词，而非「扣住」。

entries.definition: Self-control or an external limit that keeps action in check; broader and often deliberate.
entries.definitionCN: 指自我控制或外部限制，使行动受约束；更宽泛，且常是主动的。

entries.definition: Forceful putting down of a feeling, fact or activity; it stresses power and often concealment.
entries.definitionCN: 指对情绪、事实或活动的强力压下；强调权力，常含隐瞒。

entries.definition: An outside signal or action that disrupts a process rather than holding it from within.
entries.definitionCN: 指从外部扰乱过程的信号或行为，而非从内部拉住它。

entries.definition: A thing standing in the way that must be removed or gone round; it blocks movement, not a function.
entries.definitionCN: 指挡在路上、需要清除或绕开的东西；它阻碍的是移动，不是功能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin hold-in image, the real psychology and biochemistry pairs, and the real sister words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「扣住」意象、真实的心理学与生物化学搭配，以及真实的同族词。

normal.en: in- plus habere, to hold: inhibition is something held in, and the hand stops halfway.
normal.cn: in- 加 habere「握住」：抑制就是被扣在里面的东西，手停在半途。

normal.en: A car needs both an engine and a brake; a mind and a cell need inhibition too.
normal.cn: 汽车既需要引擎也需要刹车；心智与细胞同样需要抑制。

normal.en: Social inhibition, enzyme inhibition and growth inhibition are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 社交拘谨、酶抑制与生长抑制是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Remove the brake and you get the negative adjective: uninhibited, without restraint.
normal.cn: 把刹车拆掉就得到否定形容词 uninhibited，即无拘无束。

normal.en: The same noun covers a shy singer and a stopped enzyme because both are held back.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既指害羞的歌手又指被抑制的酶，因为两者都是被拉住的。

abstract.en: A brake is not a flaw in the machine; without it, every impulse becomes movement.
abstract.cn: 刹车不是机器的缺陷；没有它，每个冲动都会变成动作。

abstract.en: Inhibition is pressure applied at a distance, felt as a hand that never quite arrives.
abstract.cn: 抑制是隔着距离施加的压力，感觉像一只始终到不了的手。

abstract.en: The word hides its own paradox: what holds you back also makes steady action possible.
abstract.cn: 这个词藏着悖论：拉住你的东西，也让稳定的行动成为可能。

examples.en: Her inhibition faded once the audience began to laugh with her.
examples.cn: 观众和她一起笑起来之后，她的拘束就消散了。

examples.en: The assay measures inhibition of the enzyme at several concentrations.
examples.cn: 该检测在多个浓度下测量酶的抑制程度。

examples.en: Cultural inhibition around silence made the meeting unusually slow.
examples.cn: 围绕沉默的文化禁忌让会议异常拖沓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因希比申」——把手往回收，就是抑制

root: 来自拉丁语 inhibere「扣住、制止」← in-「在内、对着」+ habere「握住、持有」，过去分词 inhibitus，动作名词 inhibitio；经法语进入英语。来源链清楚，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from social shyness and held-back impulses to chemical, cellular, neural and medical brakes, then to taboo and stage stiffness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从社交拘谨与收住的冲动，走到化学、细胞、神经与医学上的刹车，再到禁忌与舞台上的拘束。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches for a door and stops in mid-air, held by an unseen strap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向门把，却在半空停住，被一根看不见的带子拉住。

branches.en: THE MIND'S BRAKE: shyness in company and a wish checked before it acts.
branches.cn: 心智的刹车：人前的拘谨，以及行动前被收住的愿望。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY AND THE CLINIC: reactions and secretions slowed by a substance.
branches.cn: 化学与临床：反应与分泌被某种物质减慢。

branches.en: THE CELL AND THE NERVE: growth and pain signals quieted from inside the body.
branches.cn: 细胞与神经：生长与疼痛信号在体内被压下去。

branches.en: THE SHARED TABOO: a rule that keeps a whole community from speaking.
branches.cn: 共享的禁忌：让整个群体缄口的一条规则。

branches.en: THE STRAP ON STAGE: a body that moves as if still held.
branches.cn: 舞台上的带子：身体动起来像仍被拉住。

intro.en: Inhibition is a Latin verb with an inward prefix, a holding root and an action-noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词加上内向前缀、握住词根与动作名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies habere, inhibere and inhibitio; the English family keeps the same holding image in every member.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 habere、inhibere 与 inhibitio；英语这一族的每个成员都保留同一个「握住」意象。

items.example: It turns holding into holding in.
The root is the hand that keeps the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是握着对象的那只手。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The participle supplies the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了形容词词干。

items.example: It forms the action noun.
The base English verb keeps the brake.
items.exampleCN: 英语基础动词保留了刹车。

items.example: It forms inhibited, held back in behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inhibited，指行为上受拘束。

items.example: It forms inhibitory, the technical adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成技术形容词 inhibitory。

items.example: It forms inhibitor, the substance that brakes.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inhibitor，指踩刹车的物质。

items.example: It forms uninhibited, the brake released.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 uninhibited，即刹车被放开。

由过去分词构成，义为「拘谨的」
由「起……作用」词尾构成，义为「抑制性的」
由施动者词尾构成，义为「抑制剂」
由否定前缀构成，义为「无拘无束的」

definition_zh: 最初的；开头的；（名词）首字母
definition_en: existing or happening at the beginning; also the first letter of a name
core_image: 长路尽头才有风景，但第一块路牌已经竖在脚下
scene: 报名表摊在桌上，需要填写姓名与地址。My initial reaction to the plan was cautious rather than hostile.
sceneCN: 这里 initial 是「最初的、第一反应」（第 1 个义项：发生在开头的）；句意为我对该计划的最初反应是谨慎而非敌意。图中可辨识物件：表格、钢笔、印章。

pos.zh: 形容词：最初的；开头的
名词：首字母（复数指姓名首字母）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「起初；最初」
同根动词，义为「发起；开始」
同根名词，义为「主动性；倡议」
由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「初始化」

senses.title: Happening at the beginning
senses.definition: existing or occurring at the start of a process, rather than later
senses.definitionCN: 存在于或发生在某一过程开头，而不是后来
senses.example: The initial results look promising.
senses.exampleCN: 初步结果看起来很有希望。
senses.why: Latin initium is a beginning; initial marks the door through which everything else must pass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 initium 意为「开端」；initial 标出的就是一切后续都必须经过的那道门。

senses.title: The first letter of a name
senses.definition: the first letter of a word or name, often used as a short sign of identity
senses.definitionCN: 单词或姓名的第一个字母，常用来简短标明身份
senses.example: Please write your initials in the box.
senses.exampleCN: 请在方框里写上姓名的首字母。
senses.why: The beginning of a name stands for the whole person, as the beginning of a process stands for the process.
senses.whyCN: 名字的开头代表整个人，正如过程的开始代表整个过程。

intro.en: Initial comes straight from a Latin adjective of beginning, and its noun is simply initium, a start.
intro.cn: initial 直接来自拉丁语表示「开端」的形容词，其名词原形就是 initium（开始）。

items.en: The verb inire meant "to go in, to begin", built from in- and ire "to go".
items.cn: 动词 inire 意为「进入、开始」，由 in- 与 ire「走」构成。

items.en: From inire came initium, "a beginning", and the adjective initialis, "of the beginning".
items.cn: 由 inire 得到 initium「开端」与形容词 initialis「开端的」。

items.en: The church used initials for the opening letters of a name or a book long before printing.
items.cn: 早在印刷术之前，教会就用 initials 指名字或书的开头字母。

items.en: English borrowed initial in the sixteenth century, first as an adjective in learned prose.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借用 initial，最初作为形容词出现在学术文章中。

items.en: The noun initials became common with forms and signatures, and the adjective spread to costs and results.
items.cn: 名词 initials 随表格与签名普及，形容词则扩展到成本、结果等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb for going in and beginning; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of coming first.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「进入、开始」的动词；近义组收表示「最先」的形容词。

entries.definition: The ability to act first, or a proposal that starts something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主动性、倡议」，指率先行动的能力或发起的方案。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to begin or to admit someone into a group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发起、准许加入」。

entries.definition: At first, in the opening stage.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「起初、最初」。

entries.definition: Existing from the very start and not copied.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的、原创的」，强调非复制。

entries.definition: Coming before all others, the plainest word for order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「第一的」，是最朴素的顺序词。

entries.definition: Coming before the main part, as a preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「初步的」，指正式部分前的准备。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb inire and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语动词 inire，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: inire is to go in: the beginning is the doorway you step through.
normal.cn: inire 是「走进去」：开始就是你要穿过的那道门。

normal.en: Initial, initiate, initiative and initially all share that doorway.
normal.cn: initial、initiate、initiative、initially 共享那道门。

normal.en: An initial reaction is the one you have before thinking twice.
normal.cn: initial reaction 是你再三思考之前就有的反应。

normal.en: Initial costs come before later savings.
normal.cn: 初期成本出现在后来节省之前。

normal.en: Your initials are the smallest version of your name.
normal.cn: 姓名首字母是名字最小的版本。

abstract.en: Picture the first signpost on a very long road: it is small, but it decides the direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一条极长的路上的第一块路牌：它很小，却决定了方向。

abstract.en: The initial moment is only a moment, yet it fixes what came after it.
abstract.cn: 最初的时刻只是一个瞬间，却固定了后来的一切。

abstract.en: Beginnings are agreements we make with the future before we know its terms.
abstract.cn: 开端是我们尚不知条款时与未来签下的约定。

examples.en: The initial plan had to be changed several times.
examples.cn: 最初的计划不得不改了好几次。

examples.en: Her initial answer was no, but she agreed later.
examples.cn: 她最初回答不，但后来同意了。

examples.en: Sign your initials at the bottom of each page.
examples.cn: 在每一页底部签上姓名的首字母。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你手」——一伸手就抓住最初那段

root: 拉丁语 inire「走进、开始」= in-「向内」+ ire「走」，由它派生 initium「开端」和 initialis「开端的」；同根词有 initiate、initiative、initial、initially。initials 指姓名首字母。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the adjectival sense of what comes first, and the noun for the first letter of a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：形容词表示「最先的」，名词表示姓名开头的字母。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first signpost on a long road decides which way the whole journey goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：长路上的第一块路牌决定整段旅程的方向。

branches.en: THE START: initial describes whatever exists in the opening moments.
branches.cn: 开头这条线：initial 描述存在于最初时刻的东西。

branches.en: THE SOUNDING: an initial consonant is the one heard first in a word.
branches.cn: 发音这条线：initial consonant 指词首听到的那个辅音。

branches.en: THE SIGNATURE: initials stand in for a full name on forms and letters.
branches.cn: 签名这条线：initials 在表格和信件里代替全名。

branches.en: THE MARK: a single letter can mark ownership as clearly as a whole name.
branches.cn: 标记这条线：一个字母标出所属，效果与全名相同。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in both senses the first element stands for the whole.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项里都是「最先的一小块」代表整体。

intro.en: Initial is a Latin adjective on a Latin verb of going in; English adds ordinary endings to build its family.
intro.cn: initial 是建立在拉丁语「走进」动词上的形容词，英语用普通词尾扩展成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ire, inire, initium and initialis are all recorded; only the Indo-European root of ire is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ire、inire、initium、initialis 均有记录，只有 ire 的印欧词根属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 它标出穿过门的那一步。

items.example: The verb also underlies exit and transit.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也构成 exit 与 transit。

Recorded from early Latin.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 initialis 与英语 initial。

definition_zh: 发起；开始实施；使初步了解；（经仪式）接纳为新成员
definition_en: to cause a process to begin, or to formally introduce someone into a group or skill
core_image: 第一块多米诺骨牌被手指轻轻推倒
scene: 会议室里摊开一叠项目提案，等待签字。The council voted to initiate a review of the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 initiate 是「发起、开始实施」（第 1 个义项：促使某个过程开始）；句意为议会表决通过，启动对整个体系的审查。图中可辨识物件：提案、签字笔、桌灯。

pos.zh: 动词：发起；开始实施；引导入门；接纳为成员
名词：新加入者（多见于专业书面语）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「开始；入会仪式」
同根名词，义为「主动性；倡议」
同根形容词，义为「最初的」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「发起者」

senses.title: To start a process
senses.definition: to make a process, plan, or action begin
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程、计划或行动开始
senses.example: The company initiated a new training programme.
senses.exampleCN: 公司启动了一项新的培训计划。
senses.why: Latin initiare is to begin, from initium "a beginning"; the verb names the act of opening the door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 initiare 意为「开始」，源自 initium「开端」；动词指的就是把门打开这一动作。

senses.title: To introduce someone to something new
senses.definition: to help someone learn about a subject or activity for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人第一次了解某学科或活动
senses.example: The course initiates students into the basics of law.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课引导学生进入法学的基础领域。
senses.why: To enter a new field is to be led through a beginning, so the verb means both to start and to bring someone to the start.
senses.whyCN: 进入新领域就是被带过一个开端，所以这个动词既表示开始，也表示把人领到起点。

senses.title: To admit someone by ceremony
senses.definition: to formally accept someone into a group, often with a special ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式接纳某人加入团体，常有专门仪式
senses.example: New members are initiated at the spring meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 新成员在春季会议上被正式接纳。
senses.why: Secret societies and clubs turned the doorway image into a real rite of passage.
senses.whyCN: 秘密社团与俱乐部把「门」的意象变成了真实的入会仪式。

intro.en: Initiate is the Latin verb of beginning that English borrowed for plans, lessons and ceremonies alike.
intro.cn: initiate 是拉丁语表示「开始」的动词，英语用它兼指计划、入门与仪式。

items.en: Inire, from in- and ire "to go", meant "to go in, to begin".
items.cn: inire 由 in- 与 ire「走」构成，意为「进入、开始」。

items.en: Initium, "a beginning", and the verb initiare, "to begin or admit", followed from it.
items.cn: 由它派生出 initium「开端」以及动词 initiare「开始、接纳」。

items.en: In religious use initiare meant to admit someone to the mysteries, a sacred beginning.
items.cn: 在宗教用法中 initiare 指让人进入秘仪，是一种神圣的开端。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the seventeenth century for starting actions and for formal admission.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪采用这个动词，用于发起行动与正式纳新。

items.en: Business and law now use it for launching projects and proceedings.
items.cn: 如今商业与法律领域用它表示启动项目与程序。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the root of beginning; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of starting.
note.cn: 形近组共享「开端」词根；近义组收表示「开始」的动词。

entries.definition: A proposal that starts action, or the drive to act first.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倡议、主动性」。

entries.definition: The adjective for what comes first.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的」。

entries.definition: The act of starting, or a ceremony of admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「开始、入会仪式」。

entries.definition: To start something big with publicity, like a product or a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推出、发射」，多指有声势地启动产品或船只。

entries.definition: The most general verb for starting anything.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开始」，最通用的说法。

entries.definition: To cause something to happen suddenly, like a reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引发」，强调突然触发反应。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb of beginning and the phrases the word routinely takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「开始」动词，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Initium is a beginning: to initiate is to push the first domino.
normal.cn: initium 是开端：initiate 就是推倒第一块骨牌。

normal.en: The noun initiative keeps the same root: the will to begin.
normal.cn: 名词 initiative 同根，指「开始的意愿」。

normal.en: Companies initiate projects, courts initiate proceedings.
normal.cn: 公司发起项目，法院启动程序。

normal.en: Be initiated into a club means to be let in through its door.
normal.cn: be initiated into a club 指被放进俱乐部的大门。

normal.en: An initiator is whoever acts first.
normal.cn: initiator 就是最先行动的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a finger on the first domino: everything after that is consequence.
abstract.cn: 想象手指按在第一块骨牌上：其后的一切都是后果。

abstract.en: Initiate is a choice, not an accident: someone decides the beginning will happen.
abstract.cn: initiate 是一种选择而非偶然：有人决定让开始发生。

abstract.en: Every beginning costs something, which is why starting is harder than continuing.
abstract.cn: 每个开始都有代价，这正是开始比继续更难的原因。

examples.en: The government initiated talks with the union.
examples.cn: 政府启动了与工会的谈判。

examples.en: Senior students initiate the newcomers into college life.
examples.cn: 高年级学生引导新生适应大学生活。

examples.en: The club initiated ten new members last month.
examples.cn: 俱乐部上个月正式接纳了十名新成员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你谁特」——一开始就问你是谁，然后让你入门

root: 拉丁语 inire「走进、开始」（in- + ire「走」）派生 initium「开端」与 initiare「开始、接纳」；英语十七世纪借入 initiate。同根词：initial、initially、initiative、initiation。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses all show a doorway being opened: a process begins, a learner is led in, a member is formally admitted.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在展示一扇被打开的门：过程开始、学习者被领进门、成员被正式接纳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tips the first domino and the whole line falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指推倒第一块骨牌，整排随之倒下。

branches.en: THE PROJECT: a plan or policy is initiated when someone starts it.
branches.cn: 项目这条线：方案或政策在有人启动它时被 initiate。

branches.en: THE COURT: legal action is initiated by the party who files first.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：诉讼由先提起诉讼的一方 initiate。

branches.en: THE LESSON: a teacher initiates beginners into a subject.
branches.cn: 课堂这条线：老师把初学者领进一门学科。

branches.en: THE RITE: a club initiates new members with a ceremony.
branches.cn: 仪式这条线：俱乐部用仪式接纳新成员。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense puts someone or something on the inside of a beginning.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都把人或事放到了开端的里面。

latinIntro.en: Latin inire, initium and initiare are recorded, all built on the verb ire.

senses.title: The will to act first
senses.definition: the ability and willingness to decide and act before others do, without being ordered
senses.definitionCN: 在他人之前自行决定并行动的能力与意愿
senses.example: Employers value staff who show initiative.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主看重有主动性的员工。
senses.why: Initialis describes what belongs to a beginning; initiative is the quality of making that beginning yourself.
senses.whyCN: initialis 描述属于开端的东西；initiative 则是自己做出这个开端的能力。

senses.title: A new plan put forward
senses.definition: a new plan or programme, often by a government or group, to solve a problem
senses.definitionCN: 由政府或团体提出的解决某问题的新方案或计划
senses.example: The city launched an initiative to plant more trees.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市发起了一项植树倡议。
senses.why: When a group makes the first move in public, the beginning itself is put on the table as a scheme.
senses.whyCN: 当团体公开迈出第一步，这个开端本身就作为方案摆上台面。

intro.en: Initiative is a modern noun built on the Latin adjective of beginning: the faculty of making beginnings.
intro.cn: initiative 是建立在拉丁语「开端」形容词上的现代名词，指「做出开端的能力」。

items.en: Initium, from inire "to go in", meant "a beginning"; initialis described what belongs to a beginning.
items.cn: initium 来自 inire「进入」，意为「开端」；initialis 描述属于开端的东西。

items.en: French gave the word its political form, initiative, for the right to propose a law.
items.cn: 法语赋予这个词政治形态 initiative，指提出法案的权利。

items.en: English adopted initiative in the eighteenth century in political writing about the power to propose.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪引入 initiative，用于讨论提案权的政治文献。

items.en: By the nineteenth century it also named personal drive, the habit of acting without orders.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，它也指个人干劲，即不待吩咐就行动的作风。

items.en: The twentieth century added the sense of a public campaign or programme.
items.cn: 二十世纪又增添了公共倡议或项目的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the beginning root; the near-meaning group gathers words for drive and for plans.
note.cn: 形近组共享「开端」词根；近义组收表示干劲与方案的词。

entries.definition: To start a process or admit someone to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发起、接纳」。

entries.definition: The adjective for what comes first.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的」。

entries.definition: At first, before later changes.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「起初」。

entries.definition: Inner energy that pushes a person to work hard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干劲」，指推动人努力的内在能量。

entries.definition: A plan formally suggested for others to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提议」，指正式提出供人考虑的计划。

entries.definition: Boldness in starting new things, or a business venture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进取心、事业」，兼指敢闯的精神与经营项目。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the beginning root and the fixed phrases the noun appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「开端」词根，以及这个名词的固定搭配。

normal.en: Take the initiative is the phrase to learn: nobody asks you, you move.
normal.cn: 先记住 take the initiative：没人叫你，你自己先动。

normal.en: On your own initiative means the idea was yours.
normal.cn: on your own initiative 意为这事是你自己想出来的。

normal.en: A peace initiative puts a first plan on the table.
normal.cn: a peace initiative 是把第一份方案摆上桌面。

normal.en: Initiate starts the action; initiative names the spirit behind it.
normal.cn: initiate 是开始的动作，initiative 是动作背后的精神。

normal.en: A colleague who shows initiative rarely waits to be told.
normal.cn: 表现出主动性的同事很少等着被吩咐。

abstract.en: Picture one hand raised in a room where every other hand stays down.
abstract.cn: 想象在一个所有人都垂着手的房间里，有一只手举了起来。

abstract.en: Initiative is the private decision that becomes a public beginning.
abstract.cn: 主动性是私人决定，最终成为公共的开端。

abstract.en: Energy that begins inside a person becomes motion that others can follow.
abstract.cn: 从一个人内部开始的能量，会变成别人能跟随的运动。

examples.en: She took the initiative and called the client first.
examples.cn: 她主动出击，先给客户打了电话。

examples.en: He joined the project on his own initiative.
examples.cn: 他凭自己的主动加入了该项目。

examples.en: The school started an initiative to cut food waste.
examples.cn: 学校发起了一项减少食物浪费的倡议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你谁提五」——一开始你自己提出来，就是主动性

root: initiative 源出拉丁语 initialis「开端的」（来自 initium「开端」，再上溯 inire「进入」）；法语 initiative 指提案权，十八世纪进入英语，十九世纪引申为个人干劲，二十世纪又指公共倡议。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the inner drive to act first, and the public plan that results from it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：先行行动的内在动力，以及由它产生的公开方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand goes up in a room where all other hands stay down.
core.cn: 核心意象：满屋子的手都垂着，只有一只手举了起来。

branches.en: THE PERSON: initiative is a habit of acting before being asked.
branches.cn: 个人这条线：initiative 是无需被要求就行动的作风。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: to have the initiative is to be the side that moves first.
branches.cn: 权利这条线：拥有 initiative 就是先行动的一方。

branches.en: THE CITY: a public initiative is a launched programme with a goal.
branches.cn: 城市这条线：公共 initiative 是带目标启动的项目。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the plan is placed before others for approval.
branches.cn: 桌面这条线：方案被摆到别人面前等待通过。

branches.en: THE THREAD: the private decision and the public plan are two ends of one beginning.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：私人决定与公开方案是同一个开端的两端。

intro.en: Initiative is a Latin beginning adjective with a suffix that names a quality or tendency.
intro.cn: initiative 是拉丁语「开端」形容词加表示性质与倾向的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin initium and initialis are recorded; the noun initiative itself is a later French and English formation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 initium 与 initialis 有记录；名词 initiative 本身是较晚的法语与英语构形。

items.example: The sense of beginning runs through the word.
The adjective behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是名词背后的形容词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a name for a quality.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表示性质的名词。

items.example: The action behind the quality.
The plain adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族中最朴素的形容词。

items.example: It forms initiation.
It forms initiator.
It forms initially.

definition_zh: 注射；注射剂；（资金的）注入
definition_en: the act of putting a liquid medicine into the body with a needle, or the act of adding money or energy to something
core_image: 一支针筒把药液推进皮肤下面
scene: 诊室里护士正在消毒棉球旁准备器械。The child cried for a moment, then forgot the injection entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 injection 是「注射」（第 1 个义项：用针把药液送入体内）；句意为孩子哭了一会儿，随后就完全忘了打针这回事。图中可辨识物件：针筒、棉球、消毒盘。

pos.zh: 名词：注射；注射剂；注入

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「注射；注入」
由动词加表示工具的后缀构成，义为「注射器」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「可注射的」

senses.title: Medicine put in by needle
senses.definition: the act of forcing liquid medicine into the body through a needle or tube
senses.definitionCN: 用针或导管把药液压入体内的行为
senses.example: The nurse gave him an injection in the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在他胳膊上打了一针。
senses.why: In- "into" plus iacere "to throw" gives the picture of liquid thrown into the body.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 iacere「投掷」，构成把液体投进身体的画面。

senses.title: The medicine itself
senses.definition: a measured amount of liquid medicine prepared to be injected
senses.definitionCN: 预先配好准备用于注射的一份药液
senses.example: The doctor prepared an injection of insulin.
senses.exampleCN: 医生准备了一针胰岛素。
senses.why: The act and the dose share one name, as with many medical procedures.
senses.whyCN: 动作与剂量共用一个名称，这在医疗术语中很常见。

senses.title: Money or energy added
senses.definition: the addition of money, effort, or liveliness to something that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 向欠缺之处补充金钱、努力或活力
senses.example: The cash injection saved the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资金注入救了这家工厂。
senses.why: Anything pushed forcibly into a weakened system is injected, whether serum or money.
senses.whyCN: 凡是强行推进虚弱体系的东西都算注入，无论血清还是资金。

intro.en: Injection joins a Latin prefix meaning into with a Latin verb meaning to throw.
intro.cn: injection 把拉丁语表示「向内」的前缀与表示「投掷」的动词结合起来。

items.en: Iacere meant "to throw, hurl", and it produced many verbs of projecting and sending.
items.cn: iacere 意为「投掷」，构成了许多表示投射与发送的动词。

items.en: Inicere, from in- plus iacere, meant "to throw in, insert".
items.cn: inicere 由 in- 加 iacere 构成，意为「投入、插入」。

items.en: The noun iniectio could already mean a casting in, including of fluids.
items.cn: 名词 iniectio 当时已可表示「投入」，包括液体的注入。

items.en: French injection carried the medical sense of introducing fluids.
items.cn: 法语 injection 带有引入液体的医学含义。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century; syringes made the medical sense dominant later.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入该词，后来注射器的普及使医学义成为主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of throwing; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of putting things in.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「投掷」动词；近义组收其他「放入」的说法。

entries.definition: To throw someone or something out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「弹出、驱逐」，即向外抛出。

entries.definition: To throw forward, literally or in planning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投射、规划」，即向前抛出。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to force liquid or money in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「注射、注入」。

entries.definition: A preparation given to create immunity, often by injection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疫苗」，常通过注射接种。

entries.definition: A measured quantity of medicine taken at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一剂」，指一次服用的药量。

entries.definition: Slow introduction of liquid into the body, or of new life into something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「输液、注入」，强调缓慢流入。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use iacere, the verb of throwing, and the phrases the word occurs in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用表示投掷的 iacere，以及这个词出现的搭配。

normal.en: iacere is to throw: an injection throws medicine in through a needle.
normal.cn: iacere 是「投掷」：injection 是用针把药投进去。

normal.en: Project, eject and inject all throw in different directions.
normal.cn: project、eject、inject 都是朝不同方向投掷。

normal.en: You are given an injection; you do not give it to yourself.
normal.cn: 你是被 give an injection，不会自己给自己打。

normal.en: A cash injection throws money into a struggling business.
normal.cn: cash injection 是把钱投进挣扎中的企业。

normal.en: An injector is the tool; an injection is the act.
normal.cn: injector 是工具，injection 是动作。

abstract.en: Picture liquid meeting the skin's resistance, then passing through it.
abstract.cn: 想象液体遇上皮肤的阻力，然后穿了过去。

abstract.en: Injection is a short, sharp entrance: something outside is forced inside.
abstract.cn: 注射是一次短促的进入：外面的东西被强行送到里面。

abstract.en: A system that is failing can be revived by a sudden push from outside.
abstract.cn: 一个衰败的系统可以被外界突然的一推救活。

examples.en: The doctor gave her an injection to ease the pain.
examples.cn: 医生给她打了一针以减轻疼痛。

examples.en: Two injections a day were needed at first.
examples.cn: 起初每天需要打两针。

examples.en: The company received a large cash injection from investors.
examples.cn: 公司从投资者那里获得了一大笔资金注入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因杰克逊」——因杰克逊医生打了一针，病就好了

root: 拉丁语 iacere「投掷」加 in-「向内」构成 inicere「投入」，名词 iniectio 经法语 injection 进入英语，十五世纪已有记录；同根词有 eject、project、reject、inject。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses come from one image of forcing something in: the act of injecting, the dose injected, and money or energy pushed into a system.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项出自同一个「强行送入」的意象：注射的动作、被注入的药剂，以及注入系统的金钱或活力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a syringe pushes liquid through the skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：针筒把液体推进皮肤。

branches.en: THE ACT: an injection is the moment of forcing liquid in.
branches.cn: 动作这条线：injection 是强行送入液体的那一刻。

branches.en: THE DOSE: the prepared amount is named with the same word.
branches.cn: 剂量这条线：备好的那份药液用同一个词称呼。

branches.en: THE MONEY: cash is injected into a business that needs it.
branches.cn: 资金这条线：钱被注入需要它的企业。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: new energy can be injected into a dull event.
branches.cn: 精神这条线：活力也能被注入沉闷的活动。

branches.en: THE THREAD: something from outside enters quickly and changes the state inside.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：外面的东西迅速进入并改变内部状态。

intro.en: Injection is a Latin prefix plus a Latin throwing verb, with a noun ending added along the way.
intro.cn: injection 由拉丁语前缀与「投掷」动词构成，中途加上名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin iacere, inicere and iniectio are recorded; the noun form came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iacere、inicere、iniectio 均有记录，名词形式经法语传入。

items.example: It sets the direction of the throw.
The root also gives eject and project.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 eject 与 project。

items.example: The compound behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是名词背后的复合动词。

items.example: It formed iniectio.
It forms injection.
It forms injector.
It forms injectable.
The same root with out-.

definition_zh: 使受伤；损害（名誉、感情等）
definition_en: to hurt a person or animal physically, or to damage something such as a reputation
core_image: 奔跑的人踩滑了脚，重重摔在石阶上
scene: 雨后的石阶又湿又滑，走路的人都放慢了脚步。Two players were injured in the final minutes of the match.
sceneCN: 这里 injure 是「使受伤」（第 1 个义项：造成身体上的损伤）；句意为比赛最后几分钟里有两名球员受伤。图中可辨识物件：石阶、球门、担架。

pos.zh: 动词：使受伤；损害

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「伤害；受伤处」
由过去分词转化，义为「受伤的」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「有害的；造成伤害的」

senses.title: To hurt the body
senses.definition: to cause physical harm to a person or animal, often by accident
senses.definitionCN: 使人和动物身体受到损伤，多出于意外
senses.example: He injured his knee while climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬山时伤了膝盖。
senses.why: Latin iniuria is a wrong, built from in- "not" and ius "right"; to injure is to do someone a wrong in the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iniuria 意为「不公」，由 in-「非」与 ius「法」构成；injure 就是在身体上对人做不义之事。

senses.title: To damage a reputation or feeling
senses.definition: to harm something abstract such as a reputation, an interest, or someone's pride
senses.definitionCN: 损害名誉、利益或他人自尊等抽象事物
senses.example: The rumour injured her good name.
senses.exampleCN: 这则谣言损害了她的好名声。
senses.why: The old legal sense survives here: a wrong need not leave a visible wound to count as injury.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律义在此留存：不义之事不必留下可见的伤口，也算伤害。

intro.en: Injure began as a legal word about wrongs, and only later narrowed towards bodily harm.
intro.cn: injure 最初是关于「不义」的法律词，后来才收窄到身体伤害。

items.en: Ius meant "right, law", the basis of justice and injury alike.
items.cn: ius 意为「法、权利」，justice 与 injury 都以此为基础。

items.en: Iniuria, from in- "not" plus ius, meant "injustice, a wrong done to someone".
items.cn: iniuria 由 in-「非」加 ius 构成，意为「不义、对他人施加的侵害」。

items.en: Old French injurier meant "to wrong, to insult or harm", with no physical limit.
items.cn: 古法语 injurier 意为「侵害、侮辱或伤害」，并不限于身体。

items.en: English injure first meant to wrong or insult someone, in law and in speech.
items.cn: 英语 injure 最初指在法律或言语上侵害、侮辱他人。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the bodily sense grew dominant, while damage to reputation remained.
items.cn: 十七世纪起身体受伤的义项成为主流，损害名誉的用法则保留下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin word for right and wrong; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of causing harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「法、权利」一词；近义组收表示「造成伤害」的动词。

entries.definition: The harm itself, or a place on the body that hurts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤害、伤处」。

entries.definition: Unfairness, a wrong that is not physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不公」，指非身体的侵害。

entries.definition: Causing harm, often to health or interests.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的」，多指对健康或利益。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for pain, physical or emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使疼痛、伤心」，日常用语，兼指身心。

entries.definition: To cut or break the body, typically in fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受伤」，多指打斗中造成的创口。

entries.definition: To harm things rather than people, or to harm partly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「损坏」，多用于物，且指部分损害。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the legal root of ius and the phrases the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 ius 这一法律词根，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Iniuria is a wrong: injure is to do someone a wrong in the body.
normal.cn: iniuria 是「不义」：injure 是在身体上对人行不义。

normal.en: Justice and injury share the root ius, law and right.
normal.cn: justice 与 injury 共享词根 ius，即「法、权利」。

normal.en: Players are injured; reputations can be injured too.
normal.cn: 球员会受伤，名誉也会被损害。

normal.en: The injured, used as a plural noun, means the people who were hurt.
normal.cn: the injured 作复数名词，指受伤的人们。

normal.en: An injurious habit is one that harms your health.
normal.cn: injurious habit 是损害健康的习惯。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line broken on one side: the wrong is the gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条直线被一侧破开：那道缺口就是不义。

abstract.en: An injury is a violation before it is a wound.
abstract.cn: 伤害首先是「违犯」，然后才是伤口。

abstract.en: What harms the body and what harms the name spring from the same idea of treating a person wrongly.
abstract.cn: 伤身与伤名都出自同一观念：错待一个人。

examples.en: She injured her ankle during training.
examples.cn: 她在训练中伤了脚踝。

examples.en: Three workers were injured in the accident.
examples.cn: 三名工人在事故中受伤。

examples.en: Such careless words may injure your reputation.
examples.cn: 这样轻率的话可能损害你的名誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因之」——因而受了伤，因之而伤

root: 拉丁语 ius「法、权利」加否定前缀构成 iniuria「不义」，动词 iniuriare 经古法语 injurier 变为英语 injure；同根词有 injury、injurious、justice、injustice。十七世纪后以「身体受伤」为主义。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: harm done to a body, and harm done to something as abstract as a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：对身体造成的损伤，以及对名誉这类抽象之物的损害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line of fair treatment is broken on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条公平相待的直线被一侧破开。

branches.en: THE BODY: an accident or blow injures a limb or an organ.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：事故或打击伤到肢体或器官。

branches.en: THE GAME: players are injured in sport far more often than in daily life.
branches.cn: 赛场这条线：球员在运动中受伤远比日常生活中频繁。

branches.en: THE NAME: careless words injure a reputation without leaving a mark.
branches.cn: 名誉这条线：轻率的话损害名誉而不留痕迹。

branches.en: THE FEELING: pride and trust can be injured by the same wrong.
branches.cn: 情感这条线：自尊与信任也会被同一种不义伤到。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses come from the old legal idea of doing someone a wrong.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项都源自「对他人行不义」这一古老法律观念。

intro.en: Injure is a negative Latin prefix on the word for law and right, softened by Old French.
intro.cn: injure 是「法、权利」一词加拉丁否定前缀，再经古法语软化而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius, iniuria and iniuriari are recorded, along with the related iustitia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius、iniuria、iniuriari 均有记录，还有相关的 iustitia。

definition_zh: 无罪的；清白的；无辜的；（行为）无恶意的；天真无邪的
definition_en: not guilty of a crime or wrong; also free from harm or from evil intent
core_image: 法庭上被宣判无罪的人终于抬起头，肩膀一下子松开
scene: 旁听席上有人小声议论，法槌刚刚落下。The court found him innocent of all charges.
sceneCN: 这里 innocent 是「无罪的、清白的」（第 1 个义项：未被判有罪）；句意为法庭判定他所有罪名不成立。图中可辨识物件：法槌、旁听席、卷宗。

pos.zh: 形容词：无罪的；清白的；无辜的；天真的

collocations.zh: 未经证实有罪即视为无罪

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「无罪；天真」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「无辜地；天真地」
同根形容词，义为「无害的；无恶意的」

senses.title: Not guilty
senses.definition: not guilty of a crime or of doing something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 未犯某罪或未做过错事
senses.example: She was innocent of any wrongdoing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在任何过错上都是清白的。
senses.why: Latin in- "not" plus nocere "to harm" gives "not harming"; law applies it to a person who has done no wrong.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 nocere「伤害」，意为「不伤人」；法律用它指未做过错事的人。

senses.title: Harmless to others
senses.definition: not having an evil intention, or not causing harm
senses.definitionCN: 没有恶意，或不会造成伤害
senses.example: It was an innocent question, not an accusation.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个无恶意的提问，不是指责。
senses.why: If to be innocent is to do no harm, the adjective fits words and acts as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 如果 innocent 就是「不伤人」，那么它同样适用于言语与行为。

senses.title: Free of worldly knowledge
senses.definition: having little experience of the world and no awareness of evil
senses.definitionCN: 很少接触世事，对邪恶一无所知
senses.example: An innocent child played by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 一个天真的孩子正在窗边玩耍。
senses.why: The same word links a clean record with a clean mind that has not yet met temptation.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词把清白的记录与尚未遇到诱惑的纯洁心灵连在一起。

senses.title: An innocent person hurt by chance
senses.definition: someone who suffers from an event without being responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 因事件受伤害而与事无责任关系的人
senses.example: The blast injured innocent bystanders.
senses.exampleCN: 爆炸伤及了无辜的旁观者。
senses.why: By-standers who did no wrong but suffered nonetheless are described by the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 没有过错却遭灾的旁观者，也用这同一个形容词来称呼。

intro.en: Innocent literally means "not harming", a Latin negative on the verb for doing harm.
intro.cn: innocent 字面意思是「不伤人」，是拉丁语动词「伤害」的否定形式。

items.en: Nocere meant "to hurt, injure", the source of noxious and obnoxious.
items.cn: nocere 意为「伤害」，是 noxious 与 obnoxious 的来源。

items.en: Innocens, in- "not" plus nocens "harming", meant "harmless, blameless".
items.cn: innocens 由 in-「不」加 nocens「伤害」构成，意为「无害的、无可指责的」。

items.en: Old French innocent passed the word into English with both the legal and the simple senses.
items.cn: 古法语 innocent 把这个词传入英语，法律义与朴素义并存。

items.en: English first used innocent of people who mean no harm; the legal sense followed in the courts.
items.cn: 英语最初用 innocent 指没有恶意的人，法律义随后在法庭确立。

items.en: Innocent now covers victims of accidents, harmless remarks, and childish simplicity.
items.cn: 现代英语中它能指事故受害者、无恶意的说法与稚气天真。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of harming; the near-meaning group gathers words for being blameless.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「伤害」动词；近义组收表示「无过」的词。

entries.definition: The state of being not guilty or not worldly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无罪、天真」。

entries.definition: Harmless, often in a slightly dull way.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无害的」，常略带「平淡」意味。

entries.definition: Harmful, especially to health.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的」，多指危害健康。

entries.definition: The opposite: responsible for a wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有罪的」，反义词。

entries.definition: Free of any fault, gentler than a legal verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无可指责的」，语气比法律判决温和。

entries.definition: Lacking worldly judgement, often a slight criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「天真的」，常带轻微贬义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use nocere, the Latin verb of harming, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「伤害」动词 nocere，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: No harm done: in-nocent is "not harming", and that is the whole word.
normal.cn: 没有伤害：in-nocent 就是「不伤人」，全词的精义就在这里。

normal.en: Innocent of a charge, innocent of a lie: the preposition is always of.
normal.cn: innocent of a charge、innocent of a lie：介词固定用 of。

normal.en: The legal maxim is innocent until proven guilty.
normal.cn: 法律格言是 innocent until proven guilty。

normal.en: An innocent remark is the one you did not mean to hurt with.
normal.cn: innocent remark 是你无意伤人的那句话。

normal.en: Noxious is the same root without the negative: harmful.
normal.cn: noxious 是同一词根不带否定：有害的。

abstract.en: Picture a clean sheet of paper: nothing has been written, nothing has been done.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干净的纸：什么都没写，也就什么都没做。

abstract.en: Innocence is a verdict and a state of mind at once, one given by others, one by experience.
abstract.cn: 无罪既是判决也是心态，一个由他人给出，一个由阅历决定。

abstract.en: The word protects those who never intended the harm that reached them.
abstract.cn: 这个词保护的是那些从未想过伤害、却遭到伤害的人。

examples.en: The jury declared the man innocent of all charges.
examples.cn: 陪审团宣布该男子所有罪名均不成立。

examples.en: He lost an innocent bystander in the crowd.
examples.cn: 他在人群中误杀了一名无辜的旁观者。

examples.en: Her question was innocent enough, but it embarrassed him.
examples.cn: 她的问题本无恶意，却让他很尴尬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一诺森」——一句承诺森林般清白，便是无罪的

root: 拉丁语 nocere「伤害」加否定前缀 in- 构成 innocens「不伤害的、无可指责的」，经古法语 innocent 进入英语；同根词有 innocence、innocuous、noxious。法律义与日常义并存。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: not guilty, not harmful in intent, untouched by worldly knowledge, and harmed without cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：未被判有罪、无恶意、未知世事，以及无缘无故受害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean sheet of paper on which nothing bad has been written.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张干净的白纸，上面没有写过任何坏事。

branches.en: THE COURT: a verdict of innocent ends the case against a person.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：innocent 的判决终结对某人的指控。

branches.en: THE WORD: an innocent remark was not meant to wound.
branches.cn: 言语这条线：innocent remark 本不想伤人。

branches.en: THE CHILD: innocence as a lack of knowledge of evil.
branches.cn: 孩子这条线：innocence 也指对邪恶的无知。

branches.en: THE CROWD: innocent bystanders suffer what they did not cause.
branches.cn: 人群这条线：innocent bystanders 承受了并非他们造成的后果。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense turns on the absence of harm, whether intended, done, or deserved.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都绕开「伤害」——无论是有意、已做还是应得的。

intro.en: Innocent is a Latin negative prefix on the present participle of the verb to harm.
intro.cn: innocent 是拉丁语「伤害」动词现在分词的否定形式。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nocere 与 innocens 均有记录，名词 innocentia 亦然。
